title: Reddit Is Choking Off RSS and Open Web Access to Keep AI Bots Out
snippet: Many are worried that killing RSS feeds will destroy one of the last open, user-controlled ways to read the web.
fullText:
People who post on Reddit often love to complain, especially if it’s about Reddit itself. Now they have a legit reason to do so.

The massive network of online discussion forums and social news aggregator has announced a timetable and details regarding its new antibot and data-scraping measures, which include discontinuing support for RSS feeds on Nov. 13.

The platform, which boasts over 500 million monthly active users, first hinted at these changes in early August and outlined measures it said were to protect the site from spam and to make moderation easier. But subsequent updates left users with lingering questions about when restrictions on public APIs — the rules that allow interaction between software programs — and changes to the site’s Old Reddit version would take effect.

			

More from CNET

Under the new policy, access to Old Reddit will be restricted to individuals who have used the legacy interface within the last six months. Many users still prefer this classic layout because it features fewer ads and loads faster due to its text-heavy design. As user shillyshally writes, “No geegaws, just straight up info and ads that are unobtrusive text only.”

As for slamming the door on RSS feeds, the company said those feeds have become a huge attack surface for “large-scale scraping and automated abuse,” though it will support moderators who need that option for subreddits through its developer platform. RSS is an open-web standard that lets users consume content on their own terms, without targeted ads, tracking cookies, sponsored posts or engagement-based algorithms that steer what you see.

And while it previously mentioned limiting its public API, Reddit now says it will move all public API access to its developer platform, Devvit, effectively closing the open web “front door.” That means any third-party developer accessing Reddit will need to be inside the site’s tightly controlled sandbox, barring any off-the-books workarounds or hacking.

The company said in a post on Wednesday that it’s easing the transition to its developer platform by working directly with creators to migrate over 14,000 registered apps, close technical capability gaps and help communities find new owners for abandoned bots.

A representative told CNET in an email that the company had no comment beyond the updates it had posted publicly.

Reddit frames the move as a necessary defense against abuse and theft by unauthorized AI scrapers, but some critics view it as a deliberate strategy to force users into its proprietary ecosystem. By killing open RSS feeds and shutting down public APIs, Reddit appears to be closing off ad-free, third-party alternatives that have allowed people to easily access and sort large volumes of news and messages. 

While Reddit points moderators toward internal tools like the Discord Relay app for alerts, the company says that general users relying on RSS feeds for reading Reddit content beyond moderation are out of luck: “If you use RSS for feeds outside of a community you moderate, there is no replacement. RSS has been a beloved part of the open web for a long time, and we’re grateful to everyone who used it to stay connected to Reddit.” 

Many have been quick to point out that eliminating open standards will break independent workflows and result in total platform enclosure. Users will be funneled directly into the official app and modern desktop site, where Reddit can capture ad impressions, collect usage data and ensure that its vast data — composed of many human conversations — is reserved exclusively for high-value corporate AI licensing deals with partners like Google and OpenAI.

Some users complained that Reddit’s current app and design are why they use a third-party app or still use Old Reddit. “old.reddit.com was first created in 2018,” said da_chicken, “and new reddit is still worse in every way except the lack of dark mode. You can’t compete with your own design from almost a decade ago.”

Not surprisingly, many on the RSS subreddit said they’re done with X (formerly Twitter) once RSS goes away. “I follow about 20 subs, and have nested posts/threads I subscribe to if I find something interesting and want to see replies. Without RSS, I don’t see how the site is even usable,” wrote way-too-lazy.

One user suggested reaching far back into internet history to replace Reddit. “Maybe we should go back to DIGG. Are they still around?” asked OneCalledWell.

title: Audible Will Soon Let You Use AI to Talk to a Book Character
snippet: Amazon’s audiobook service is rolling out new AI-powered features to make listening to stories more interactive.
fullText:
Audible is making audiobook listening more immersive. The Amazon-owned streaming service launched three new AI-powered features on Thursday to expand the book-listening experience. You’ll be able to explore character guides, interact with stories and access bonus content to learn more about cities and landmarks referenced in the book you’re listening to.

Yes, this means the ability to hold a conversation with a book’s character is on the horizon. Generative AI is the tool that’s powering the Interactive Story feature. Users will soon be able to engage, for instance, with Count Dracula’s rat-eating manservant, Renfield, through a new interactive story.

According to Audible, the interactive nature of this feature is guided by the creators and publishers of the titles it’ll be featured on, thus keeping the narrative grounded and believably connected to the events in the book. (Audible didn’t say who guides the feature on books by dead authors like Dracula’s Bram Stoker.)

			

More from CNET

“The character speaks first, assigning the listener a role, goal, and stakes; the listener responds in their own words, and the character reacts in real time,” Audible explains.

Audible’s new interactive AI features — Interactive Story, Character Guide and Visual Explorer — will expand your audiobook listening experience.Audible

I went looking for this interactive story as a chapter in Dracula, a new Audible Original that premiered Thursday, but Renfield on the Run was nowhere to be found. Perhaps the rollout of this feature will take some time for users to access with this title. I’m on an Android phone, so that may also be an issue.

The press release says these new AI features are in beta testing and will be rolling out in a limited capacity for customers in the US and UK.

An Audible spokesperson didn’t immediately respond to our request for further comment.

What I did find in Dracula, though, was the newly launched Character Guide feature, which tracks the speaking character in real time and offers an information card with details about the performer playing the role. It’s all on the player page, minimizing distractions.

The character guide feature is now available for George Orwell’s 1984 and will be part of Audible’s upcoming original audiobook Exoplanet, written by Benjamin Percy and executive-produced by Project Hail Mary author Andy Weir. Audible plans to expand this feature to let listeners interact with the guide and ask questions as the story progresses.

Visual Explorer has yet to launch, but this feature will provide listeners with additional imagery and visual context for locations and important moments featured in a given narrative. 

“These new features invite listeners into a story in ways that simply weren’t possible before, marking the latest step in our nearly 30-year journey to push audio storytelling forward,” Audible’s Chief Content Officer Rachel Ghiazza said in a statement.

title: Amazon releases its own Jev clone as decision models flood the web
snippet: Amazon Web Services' Strand Labs has released the latest Jevalike decision model, Strands Decider 2B.
fullText:
Amazon Web Services released an open source decision model inspired by TypeSafe’s Jev, with AI developers increasingly seeking intelligence that is more suited to computer automation than frontier LLMs.

Amazon’s Strands Decider 2B, released the same week OpenAI announced a similar offering, is a high-speed, low-cost way to sort between pre-decided options and deliver a measure of how confident it is in its choice. The model is fully open sourced, available now, and small enough to run locally.

Amazon distinguished engineer Marc Brooker came up with the project after seeing Jev and trying to build his own take on such a model. The homebrew project was successful enough — it briefly reached the top spot on the Jevbench ranking for models of its size — that Amazon engineers cleaned it up and released it as an offering from their Strands Labs, an organization developing new tools and protocols for deploying AI agents.

Brooker says the need for a tool like this emerged in conversations with AWS customers, whose agentic workflows didn’t always require the capability or cost of a fully featured LLM all the time.

“What originally piqued my interest in this class of models was that they make a perfect decider for a workflow step — ‘what is the next thing for me to do here, based on where I am?’” Brooker told TechCrunch. He said it offers customers “a workflow step that can be structured in a way that is more reliable, thanks to the confidence scores, thanks to the closed domain of answers, [and is] lower latency, potentially lower cost.”

Like other decision models, Strands Decider is built on the “torso” of an LLM, in this case Qwen3.5-2B, but instead of generating text, it delivers calibrated choices. TypeSafe named their model Jev after the economist William Stanley Jevons, with hopes of invoking his theory that the falling cost of something — like computer intelligence — can, in fact, increase its demand.

The fact that dozens of similar models have been produced by researchers since TypeSafe debuted its idea shows the wide interest, but also raises the question of how valuable they can be. Brooker suggests that the challenge will be in optimizing the model’s speedy decision-making without compromising its intelligence.

“There is a very careful balance to be found where you want to push its performance on accuracy and calibration on these kinds of tasks, without degrading its performance on understanding different languages, on having the kind of knowledge it has, which is what makes it general purpose and interesting and useful,” he told TechCrunch. 

Still, he doesn’t necessarily expect the frontier labs to dominate the space, especially since, with smaller markets, the cost to build something interesting is in the hundreds or thousands of dollars.

For their part, TypeSafe executives say they are keeping their heads down and improving future models.

“I get that people think it’s a gold rush, but they might be underestimating the difficulty of making the models actually smart,” CEO and founder Diogo Almeida told TechCrunch, saying that for now, he didn’t see real competition for his company emerging yet. 

“The current batch seems more like ML people wanting to implement a cool architecture than a team deeply dedicated to making intelligence useful.”

title: Which Privacy and Security Apps Do You Trust the Most?
snippet: Do you use a VPN, antivirus or other security software? Let us know which ones are the most trustworthy.
fullText:
Security software works quietly in the background, so it’s easy to forget about it until something goes wrong. If you use it to keep your devices safe, we want to know about it. Does it effectively catch threats without slowing down your computer? Or has it earned a spot as something you can’t live without?

CNET’s People’s Picks survey gives you a chance to share what you think about products and services you use daily. During the month of October, we want to know which security software you rely on most to keep your devices protected. You can take our two-minute survey to share your thoughts on its threat protection, ease of use, impact on device performance, value and overall satisfaction. The top picks will make it into our roundup, so be sure to check in next month to see the winners.

Why we want to hear from you

How a security suite performs day-to-day and how it affects your device are things that only real-world users like you can give us insights into.

			

More from CNET

“Privacy and security services are constantly evolving to meet users’ demands,” says Moe Long, CNET’s senior editor for privacy and security suites. “Just as I — and likely many of you — value trust and transparency from these privacy and cybersecurity services, so too do we value your experience with software. We’re keen to learn about how you, our readers, protect your data and devices.”

Whether you’re using a free built-in option or a premium suite, you can help other CNET readers find protection that’s actually worth trusting by sharing your thoughts.

How to make your voice heard

The survey will be open through October and takes only a few minutes to complete. After we gather enough responses. We’ll crunch the numbers and publish a roundup of the winners that CNET readers rated highly.

Need a refresher? Check out which VPNs, password managers, ID theft and data-removal services our experts recommend.

title: WhatsApp expands parental controls to teen accounts with group alerts, Meta AI restrictions
snippet: After introducing parent-managed accounts for pre-teens earlier this year, WhatsApp today expanded its parental controls to teen accounts, adding group activity alerts and additional restrictions for Meta AI. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
After introducing parent-managed accounts for pre-teens earlier this year, WhatsApp today expanded its parental controls to teen accounts, adding group activity alerts and additional restrictions for Meta AI. Here are the details.

WhatsApp expands parental control options

Earlier this year, WhatsApp announced a series of new features aimed at giving parents more control over their pre-teens’ accounts.

That included letting parents decide who can contact the account and which groups it can join, review message requests from unknown contacts, and manage its privacy settings, with changes protected by a parent-set PIN.

Then, a few weeks ago, WhatsApp further expanded the feature on iOS by adding a dedicated “Parental controls” section to the Settings app, making it easier for parents to find and set up a managed account.

Today, WhatsApp expanded those controls yet again, this time bringing parental controls to teens rather than just pre-teens, while giving parents more visibility into group activity and more say over how their teens interact with Channels, Status updates, and, perhaps more importantly, Meta AI.

With the update, parents can now receive notifications when their teen joins or leaves a group, as well as when a group they are already in “grows meaningfully in size.” Parents can now also choose how their teen can use Channels, whose Status updates they can see, and who is allowed to see their own.

As for Meta AI, parents can now choose between the standard experience designed for users aged 13 and up, or a stricter “Limited Content” option, depending on what they consider appropriate for their teen.

According to WhatsApp, the Limited setting further restricts the topics a teen can discuss with Meta AI. Meta AI features that rely on Private Processing are also unavailable when the setting is enabled.

As before, WhatsApp notes that these parental controls do not give parents access to their teen’s actual messages or calls, which remain protected by end-to-end encryption.

fullText:
Amazon is calling for people to support AI data center projects, or risk irreparable harm to the US economy and national security. In a more than 3,000 word blog posted today, Amazon web services CEO Matt Garman pushed back on public concerns around the impact that data centers may have on jobs, power demands, and the environment, saying “our nation can’t afford to lose” the race for AI dominance.

“With any change, there will be important questions raised, but there will also be misinformation and outright lies, and in the age of social media and 24/7 news, myths take hold faster than ever before,” said Garman. “In fact, this build out is so important geopolitically that there are widespread reports of various countries intentionally seeding misinformation in the US about data centers to trick us into slowing down.”

This comes as support for AI data centers has plummeted in polls, and face increasing backlash from the US communities where they’re being built, with nationwide concerns growing over AI safety and what impact the technology will have on society if left unchecked.

“Right now there are over 100 data center moratoriums being considered across the country,” said Garman. “If these measures are enacted, the US could be writing its own losing ticket to this race, and the consequences would last generations.”

The lengthy memorandum includes a list of practices that Amazon is codifying under a “Data Center Commitment,” around things like creating jobs, preventing increases to local energy rates, and pledging to invest more than $1 billion to support communities that neighbor its data centers. Additionally, Amazon says it no longer uses nondisclosure agreements with government agencies, after Democratic lawmaker Jamie Raskin probed tech companies about the secret deals with local officials.

In an interview about the nondisclosure agreements reported by the The Wall Street Journal, Amazon chief global affairs and legal officer David Zapolsky said “the industry comes from a history of secrecy and so some of that’s just reflex.” He added that community leaders need to share information with their constituents, and that “It just didn’t make sense” to require secrecy anymore.

title: Samsung reportedly confirms November launch for first Android XR glasses
snippet: Samsung has apparently confirmed a November 2026 launch for its first Android XR smart glasses. more…
fullText:
Samsung has apparently confirmed a November 2026 launch for its first Android XR smart glasses.

The Korea Herald cites a “Samsung official” who confirmed that the company will be launching its Android XR glasses in November. A specific release date was not confirmed, nor any details about if there’s a full launch event or not for Samsung’s Android XR glasses.

The report reiterates that the first releases are display-less glasses similar to Meta’s Ray-Ban glasses and that they will have a camera. Samsung has shown off these models over the course of 2026, most notably around its Galaxy Z Fold 8 launch event in July where designs from Warby Parker and Gentle Monster were both on display.

Also mentioned is that Samsung is apparently targeting weight “up to 5 grams” lighter than Meta’s base Ray-Ban model (51g).

	

Pricing remains unclear.

title: Medical records giant Epic pauses product development to fix security bugs that risk patients’ data
snippet: The health tech software giant, which makes the widely used MyChart system for accessing medical data, will focus on fixing security bugs for the next few weeks.
fullText:
Epic, the software technology giant that makes the widely used MyChart software for accessing patients’ medical data, has paused most of its product development as the company works to protect its software and systems from cyberattacks.

Judy Faulkner, the founder and chief executive of Epic, told Modern Healthcare last month that the pause would likely last six weeks while work continues on “safeguarding” the company’s products, after a deployment of Anthropic’s frontier cybersecurity model Mythos unearthed security flaws that could allow access to patients’ data.

The company has not disclosed the nature of the bugs, but its chief security officer Stirling Martin told The New York Times that some customer configurations of MyChart could allow outsiders to access patient records without recording any intrusion in the software’s logs.

Martin, who did not return TechCrunch’s request for comment, told the Times that the AI model did not say if the bug could be exploited to alter patient records without detection, but argued it was enough of a risk to remediate the issues.

Epic’s widely used MyChart software is used to maintain over 320 million patient records across hospitals and doctor’s offices across the United States. Epic says it does not have access to customers’ medical data: that responsibility falls on healthcare providers like hospitals and doctor’s offices. But a bug unknown to Epic could allow hackers to compromise multiple MyChart affected systems located across the United States and raid the data stored within.

It’s rare for a company to pause development to fix security bugs, but the advent of AI tools capable of rapidly finding and exploiting security vulnerabilities has led to concerns that attackers could have an easier time at stealing data.

Healthcare breaches are increasingly common as hackers seek access to highly sensitive health and medical data, under the assumption that providers would pay to prevent hackers from publishing the information online. A 2024 ransomware attack on Change Healthcare, a health tech company owned by insurance giant UnitedHealth tasked with handling payments and billing for most Americans, allowed hackers to steal health data on more than 192 million people, the majority of people in the United States. The company paid the hackers twice not to publish the stolen data.

This year, a string of back-to-back data breaches at healthcare and tech companies have affected tens of millions of Americans. This includes medical records stolen during a breach at electronic health data storage giant CareCloud, millions of rows of patient data from pharmaceutical distributor McKesson, and an unspecified amount of stolen data from U.K.-based health tech company Craneware, whose software is used across North America. 

The Department of Health and Human Services currently lists a breach at dental insurance company DentaQuest affecting 15 million people as the largest healthcare-related data breach of 2026 so far.

fullText:
Nearly a decade in, foldables have come a long way. Even Apple has noticed all of the fun Android users are having with their bendable smartphones, jumping into the crowd with next month’s iPhone Duo. Unfortunately, you usually need to break an arm and a leg to afford one, but with this one-day-only deal on the last-gen Galaxy Z Fold 7 at Amazon, your entry fee to the foldable club is down to the price of modern slab flagships. You’ll need to hurry though, as this deal is already halfway to selling out.

Amazon is selling Samsung’s excellent 2025 foldable flagship Galaxy Z Fold 7 unlocked for just $1,350 today, reduced even further from the ~$1,500 price point it’s held since its successors launched in mid-summer. This model comes in just a single colorway and storage combination — mint, 256GB — but assuming you aren’t picky, it’s a great price for a foldable that really doesn’t feel all that last-gen in your daily life.

Buy Galaxy Z Fold 7 at Amazon for $1,350

While this year’s Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra acts as a successor to this model, what’s actually improved on the 2026 release makes for a pretty short list. Sure, the upgrade from the Snapdragon 8 Elite to the 8 Elite Gen 5 is nice to see, and the brighter, anti-reflective main display is hard to argue with. But really, the only big difference between the two is the Fold 8 Ultra’s larger 5,000mAh silicon-carbon battery. You’ll have to settle for a smaller 4,400mAh cell — along with slower 25W charging speeds — though that should be enough to get you through all but your most taxing of days.

Even with a couple of minor sacrifices, considering the way smartphone prices are trending, scoring a foldable for just $50 more than Samsung’s Galaxy S26 Ultra is hard to argue with. Amazon also supports trade-ins, meaning Pixel and Galaxy users can save up to a further $575 on the total price. It might not have that fancy anti-reflective display or a silicon-carbon battery — nor does it have the passport shape seen on the base Fold 8 — but for $1,350, it’s the best deal we’ve seen on a foldable in a while. You’ll have to hurry though, as this deal only goes until the end of today, or until sold out.

title: Welcome to Opt Out October: It’s Time to Ditch Unwanted Subscriptions and AI Spies
snippet: It’s a good month to reassess old accounts and retake control of your data and privacy.
fullText:
Tired of companies constantly updating their terms and conditions to train their AI with your data, recruit your personal info for their own ends, or charge ever-higher fees? On Thursday, the Electronic Frontier Foundation launched its 2026 Opt Out October guide, urging people to retake control of their data and devices.

If you’ve been wanting to change your privacy settings, stop social media from looking over your shoulder and avoid age verification requirements, this is the guide to start with. The EFF guide walks through all the toggles to flip and the platforms or services you should outright avoid, suggesting better alternatives where available.

The EFF notes on its blog that it will update the guide’s instructions and details if anything changes.

			

More from CNET

A representative from the EFF didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.  

What should I be opting out of?

Find privacy suggestions and alternatives to common choices.Screenshot by Stephen Shankland/CNET

EFF’s Opt Out October focuses on services that have been shown to treat your personal data poorly, and there are a lot of options. 

My personal favorite is the AI tools section, which teaches you how to stop chatbots and platforms like Twitch and Snapchat from training on your data.

title: World’s first enhanced geothermal power plant completed in just 23 months
snippet: Fervo Energy completed its first power plant in less than two years. The next phases promise to connect to the grid even quicker.
fullText:
Geothermal company Fervo Energy announced Thursday morning that it had started selling electricity from its Cape Station power plant to the grid on September 30, one day ahead of schedule.

With it, Fervo becomes the first enhanced geothermal company to reach a key commercial milestone. The power plant synchronized with the grid about a week ago, bringing online the first third of what will soon become a 100-megawatt power plant.

The entire site could be much larger, though, with the potential to generate as much as 4 gigawatts of electricity, Fervo previously told TechCrunch.

“No team has ever built a project like this anywhere in the world, and we did it ahead of schedule,” Fervo co-founder and CEO Tim Latimer said in a statement.

From groundbreaking to commercial operations, the first block at Cape Station took 23 months to complete. As Fervo refines its process, it is aiming to complete future blocks in as little as 18 months.

That sort of speed to power should appeal to power-starved data center operators, who have been scouring every part of the energy sector for generating capacity. Geothermal can also be developed in phases, similar to how data centers are developed, allowing hyperscalers to bring racks online as demand ramps up.

Google, Southern California Edison, and others have committed to buying power from Fervo’s Cape Station project, which is located in Utah. 

Fervo is one of several companies developing enhanced geothermal power plants. While traditional geothermal power taps heat sources close to the surface, Fervo and its peers are drilling deeper because deeper rock is hotter, opening more opportunities for development. 

Fervo went public in May in an upsized IPO that raised $1.9 billion. It was founded in 2017, bringing drilling techniques and technologies from the oil and gas sector to the development of new geothermal resources. As a startup, the company raised more than $1.3 billion from investors, including Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Congruent Ventures, and Capricorn Investment Group.

title: GrayKey maker can reportedly bypass the iPhone’s ‘Inactivity Reboot’ security feature
snippet: As reported by 404 Media, Magnet Forensics says it has found a way to bypass the iPhone security feature that automatically reboots devices if they haven’t been unlocked for 72 hours. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
As reported by 404 Media, Magnet Forensics says it has found a way to bypass the iPhone security feature that automatically reboots devices if they haven’t been unlocked for 72 hours. Here are the details.

A bit of context

Nearly two years ago, the iOS 18.1 update introduced Inactivity Reboot, a feature that forces iPhone reboots in case they haven’t been unlocked for 72 hours.

In essence, this feature makes it harder for law enforcement and forensic tools to access data on a locked iPhone, since a reboot causes the device to return to a Before First Unlock (BFU) state, rather than remaining in the less restrictive After First Unlock (AFU) state.

When an iPhone is in BFU, certain sensitive data remains protected by encryption keys that only become available after the user enters their passcode for the first time, thus putting the device in AFU.

From that point on, more of the device’s data remains accessible until the iPhone is rebooted again, which returns it to BFU.

Automatically rebooting an iPhone means that even if a device is seized by law enforcement, it can return to BFU before investigators can access it, since obtaining a warrant or transporting the device to a forensic lab can take time.

As 404 Media noted when iOS 18.1 was released, the feature can also make it harder for thieves or other bad actors to keep a stolen iPhone in AFU long enough to develop or use a way to break into it.

GrayKey reportedly gets around Inactivity Reboot

404 Media reported today that, based on an “educational and tutorial video, which was made exclusively for law enforcement agents and appears to be dated early 2025,” Magnet Forensics, the company behind the GrayKey phone unlocking tool, appears to have developed a way to bypass the iPhone’s Inactivity Reboot feature.

According to the report, Magnet developed a new device called GrayKey Preserve, as well as an Evidence Preservation Mode for its existing GrayKey hardware.

Both are reportedly designed to maintain an iPhone’s forensic state without immediately exposing the data stored on the device, allowing law enforcement to keep that state intact while waiting for authorization to search it.

The report notes that while the video doesn’t detail the technical mechanism behind the workaround, it explains that GrayKey can preserve an iPhone’s AFU state even if the device reboots.

From the report:

“That AFU state is captured,” by GrayKey Preserve and Evidence Preservation Mode, the employee says. “Even if that device does reboot for any number of reasons, memory maintenance or the power is lost or whatever, the AFU state is not lost. This is the true magic behind the GrayKey Preserve and the Evidence Preservation Mode function.”

404 Media reached out to Apple and Magnet Forensics, but neither responded to a request for comment. They also consulted iPhone security researcher Jiska Classen, who said Magnet may have found a way to manipulate the iPhone’s clock, or to turn off the processes responsible for expiring certain data altogether.

While the video appears to date from early 2025, it is unclear how long the technology has been available to law enforcement, whether it has been used in actual investigations, or whether the workaround remains effective against the latest versions of iOS.

title: Robotaxi operators will face fines for blocking first responders
snippet: A new California law places new rules on autonomous vehicles operators.
fullText:
Autonomous vehicle (AV) technology companies like Tesla, Waymo, and Zoox will have to provide first responders with local, on-the-ground support when their robotaxis cause problems under a new California law. The companies could also face penalties if a robotaxi blocks police or firefighters for more than 30 minutes.

Senate Bill 1246, which was signed into law by Gov. Gavin Newsom, sets a series of new rules for AVs designed to improve safety and response times when they become disabled or interfere with emergency responders. The law also creates ways to hold these companies accountable if they don’t.

The law follows a string of high-profile incidents in California in which robotaxis broke down and disrupted traffic, drove into crime scenes, or impeded first responders.

The bulk of those incidents involved Waymo, the largest robotaxi operator in the U.S. , which has about 4,000 autonomous vehicles in its commercial fleet across the country. About 1,200 of those are in the San Francisco Bay Area. A TechCrunch investigation earlier this year identified a number of incidents in which Waymo relied on first responders to manually drive its vehicles when they encountered problems.

Those incidents prompted state and federal lawmakers to call for stricter rules governing robotaxis, particularly how they behave around first responders. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) even sent a letter to AV developers demanding that they come up with “solutions” to the problem.

This new California law attempts to address those concerns, at least in the state.

“California has embraced autonomous vehicles, but we cannot embrace innovation at the expense of public safety. When an autonomous vehicle crashes, breaks down, blocks a roadway in an emergency, or gets in the way of law enforcement or first responders, there must be clear accountability,” said state Senator Dave Cortese, who introduced the bill. 

Under the law, AV developers can only employ remote drivers who are based in the United States and those drivers must hold a U.S. driver’s license. The requirement is meant to address concerns around how companies use remote operations when autonomous vehicles run into trouble.

The term “remote operations” has been interpreted very broadly and there is still little known about the methods AV companies use. The “remote drivers” term in the law is far more specific. It refers to a human who directly operates or drives the vehicle from afar. Tesla is the only company that has publicly stated that it has remote operators who can take direct control of its robotaxis.

Other companies, including Waymo, have said they use forms of remote assistance, in which the self-driving system remains in control and a human employee can provide guidance or send software commands if needed. Waymo has a global network of remote assistance staff, including in the Philippines, and operates command centers in Arizona and Michigan. Zoox’s remote operations teams are based in the United States, according to the company. 

The law will also require AV companies to notify cities, towns, and other local jurisdictions about the location and status of vehicles during system-wide failures and to provide “local incident technicians” who can assist with AV accidents and obstructions. Companies can also be fined if an AV blocks first responders during an emergency for more than 30 minutes.

Companies including Waymo and Zoox have said they will comply.

“We are grateful for the amendments made to the bill, which ensure autonomous vehicle operators can still feasibly serve Californians,” a Waymo spokesperson said in an emailed company statement. “Waymo is committed to making roads safer in California and continually improving our service.”

The law goes into effect in July 2028. The California Department of Motor Vehicles, which regulates autonomous vehicles in the state, will set guidelines on certain aspects of the new law, including required response times.

title: Tesla’s recovery hits a speed bump
snippet: Tesla sold fewer vehicles in the third quarter than it did a year ago, when consumers rushed to cash in on expiring federal tax credits for electric vehicle purchases. But the company still beat estimates from Wall Street, suggesting that it's recovery was still on track. Tesla said that it produced a total of 464,391 vehicles between July and September of this year, including 457,387 Model 3 and Model Y vehicles, as well as 7,004 "other vehicles" like the Cybertruck, Cybercab, and Tesla Semi. fullText:
Tesla sold fewer vehicles in the third quarter than it did a year ago, when consumers rushed to cash in on expiring federal tax credits for electric vehicle purchases. But the company still beat estimates from Wall Street, suggesting that it’s recovery was still on track.

Tesla said that it produced a total of 464,391 vehicles between July and September of this year, including 457,387 Model 3 and Model Y vehicles, as well as 7,004 “other vehicles” like the Cybertruck, Cybercab, and Tesla Semi. (The company discontinued the Model S and X earlier this year.) That represents about a 3.8 percent increase compared to the third quarter of 2025, when the company produced 447,450 vehicles.

Tesla also said that it delivered to customers a total of 486,532 vehicles, including 481,166 Model 3 and Model Y vehicles, as well as 8,295 other vehicles — about a 2.1 percent decrease compared to the blockbuster third quarter of 2025, when it delivered 497,099 vehicles. (For a direct-to-consumer company like Tesla, deliveries are a proxy for sales.)

The drop in sales was widely expected thanks to the expiration of the $7,500 federal tax credit for electric vehicles on September 30, 2025. Elon Musk himself said that the company was in for “a few rough quarters” thanks to the expiring incentive and other macroeconomic factors.

But Musk also said he believes that Tesla will rebound as its AI plans come to fruition, including robotaxis and humanoid robots. We saw how that might play out, with the July launch of the steering-wheel and pedal-less Cybercab in Austin. Even so, Musk predicted that 50 percent of the US population will have access to Tesla’s robotaxis by the end of 2025 — which of course turned out to be very wrong.

Last quarter, Tesla said its sales were up 25 percent year over year. Wall Street investors were expecting Tesla to report sales of 463,000 vehicles for the second quarter. The company-compiled sell-side analyst consensus estimated 461,974 vehicle deliveries for Q3. Today’s report represents a clean beat of those expectations.

The report comes amid a tumultuous time for Tesla — which always seems to be the case for any company with Elon Musk at the helm. The company scored some good headlines — the re-launch of the Semi and Cybercab, European sales rebound, a boost in EV market share stateside — and was rocked by a few bad ones — the delay of the next-gen Roadster reveal and a federal investigation into the Cybercab launch.

title: Pixel 10a gets a $100 price hike, now starting at $599
snippet: Google has quietly raised the price of its mid-range Pixel 10a by $100, giving the device a starting price of $599. more…
fullText:
Google has quietly raised the price of its mid-range Pixel 10a by $100, giving the device a starting price of $599.

Effective as of today at the Google Store, Pixel 10a has jumped from $499 to $599. The reason is obvious, of course, with the current skyrocketing costs of components such as memory. Google has not officially commented on the price hike yet, though.

This follows Google issuing a price increase to each of its new Pixel 11 devices compared to the prior generation. 

When Google confirmed the Pixel 11 would be more expensive, the company said that this would eventually impact “in-market Pixel phones” which, at the time, we speculated could include Pixel 10a.

	

The 128GB base Pixel 10a is $599 as of today, with the 256GB model at $699. The updated prices have already kicked in at Amazon and Best Buy.

In our review of Pixel 10a, we called the device a “well-rounded experience” for its $499 price, but a $100 jump certainly makes that a tougher conversation, especially considering Google’s mid-ranger is at this point using a two-generation-old chipset in its Tensor G4. title: The Pixel 3a might be the most important Google smartphone to date
snippet: Google Pixel was designed to be a premium smartphone effort, but that all changed in 2019 with the debut of the Pixel 3a. The budget-conscious launch went on to be a turning point for the Pixel’s history and, looking back, it might just be the single most important Google smartphone ever. more…
fullText:
Google Pixel was designed to be a premium smartphone effort, but that all changed in 2019 with the debut of the Pixel 3a. The budget-conscious launch went on to be a turning point for the Pixel’s history and, looking back, it might just be the single most important Google smartphone ever.

Looking back over the past decade of Pixel smartphones, I’m not sure you can point at any one device and say it was more important than the Pixel 3a. The original Pixel set the foundation, of course, and Pixel 6 launched Google’s efforts into a new era, but Pixel 3a gave Google a taste of what it was always after – market success.

The Pixel 3a almost immediately shot up to the top of best-seller lists, massively propelled Google’s US smartphone sales, and was the driving force behind setting Google’s first big shipment records. That success ultimately led to several Pixel A-series successors that have similarly resonated in the market. These more affordable devices just nail the fundamentals at a price that’s hard to beat, especially considering the cost of a Pixel 10a is only $100 more (annnnnnd now it’s $200) than the Pixel 3a originally started at.

Google is finding at least some success in the flagship market nowadays. Pixel phones are very much hitting their stride in 2026 not only in terms of design and functionality, but also in the market as a whole. I’d very much argue, though, that the Pixel 3a was the lifejacket that kept this project going. The failure of the Pixel 4 left scars on Google’s smartphone efforts, but the Pixel 3a’s resounding success was surely a huge deciding factor on what would come next.

	

And, in 2026, I think this phone holds up remarkably well from a hardware perspective. There are modern budget phones that cost just as much as the Pixel 3a did when it came out that feel a lot worse than this one. The Pixel 3a is long dead at this point with software support having ended in 2022, but its legacy lives on.

title: OpenAI launches Dots, new ‘always-on agents’ you can assign tasks to
snippet: Right as Meta’s Muse avatar agent has taken the AI world by storm, OpenAI is today announcing Dots as “always-on agents” you can customize to your needs. more…
fullText:
Right as Meta’s Muse avatar agent has taken the AI world by storm, OpenAI is today announcing Dots as “always-on agents” you can customize to your needs.

Out of OpenAI DevDay 2026, Dots are OpenAI’s answer to giving users a way to assign tasks to an AI agent to run in the background. The company says that Dots, powered by GPT-6 Astra, has “their own cloud computer” and can use that to accomplish tasks that you have assigned. You can interact with Dots via ChatGPT, Slack, or Teams once they’ve been set up.

OpenAI explains:

Dots are frontier intelligence that have your back. Powered by GPT‑6 Astra, they have their own cloud computer, learn from feedback over time, and can work towards your goals 24/7. Through our ecosystem of plugins, they can readily connect to over 4,000 apps, giving them the tools to help wherever you need them.

Your dot is always within reach, whether it is through ChatGPT, Slack, or Teams. You can ask questions, explore ideas, and give feedback along the way; or you can simply hop on a voice call when you need to talk something out. The more you work together, the more your dot learns your preferences, how you think, and what good looks like to you.

Some examples of how OpenAI says it is using Dots internally include having Dots automatically investigate bugs when they are mentioned in Slack, creating working apps when a “new design” is ready, and more. Another example saw a Dot notice on its own that an invoice had not been sent, to which it created that invoice for the user’s approval. Dots do “proactive research” when not actively working on a task through read-only connections with tools you’ve connected.

	

As the user, you can see a Dot’s cloud computer at any time while it is working on a task, as well as giving it permission to use your computer. 

OpenAI further adds that Dots follow the same permissions and controls as ChatGPT, and they also support custom rules around when they can act on their own or require approval from you. 

Dots are available today to Pro and Business Premium users, with Enterprise users also able to try it out when workspace admins approve it. One Dot is included with these plans, with OpenAI saying you’ll be able to add more in the future. Dots must be created via the ChatGPT desktop app or browser, but can be interacted with via the mobile app after that.

title: Audible announces AI-powered character guides, interactive stories, more
snippet: Audible today announced three features coming to “deepen customers’ connections to their favorite stories.” Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Audible today announced three features coming to “deepen customers’ connections to their favorite stories.” Here are the details.

Audible announces Character Guides

Starting today, Audible users listening to the Audible Original Bram Stoker’s Dracula audiobook will be able to access Character Guide, right from the player page.

This is a new feature that shows who is speaking in real time, and provides spoiler-free cards with details about each character and the performer behind each voice, “complete with narrator headshots and bios.”

Audible adds that, coming soon, Character Guide will also allow listeners to ask questions about the production as the story unfolds.

Character Guide is also available with Audible’s adaptation of George Orwell’s 1984, and will be included with Benjamin Percy’s Exoplanet when it launches on November 5.

Two more features coming soon

In addition to Character Guide, Audible today announced two other AI-powered features: Interactive Story and Visual Explorer.

Audible describes Interactive Story as a “bonus experience beyond the original narrative,” explaining that it will allow users to have real-time conversations with characters from supported audiobooks.

Here’s Audible:

The first Interactive Story accompanies the Audible Original Bram Stoker’s Dracula and follows the character of Renfield, Dracula’s unpredictable, tormented servant. The character speaks first, assigning the listener a role, goal, and stakes; the listener responds in their own words, and the character reacts in real time.

The platform notes that creators have control over multiple aspects of the interaction, and adds that after Dracula, Benjamin Percy’s Audible Original Exoplanet will get the new experience.

As for Visual Explorer, Audible says it will “surface relevant imagery and visual context at key moments during listening,” whether it’s a map to help listeners better visualize where the story is unfolding, or an image “tied to a pivotal moment” in the narrative.

Visual Explorer is coming soon, with Audible highlighting The Cultural Tutor’s Grand Tour: The Story of Europe in Six Cities as one title featuring the experience, while Interactive Story is “rolling out this fall.”

title: Nvidia Shield TV Pro is now $299 – a $100 price hike seven years after the Android TV box launched
snippet: The Nvidia Shield TV is an iconic piece of Android hardware but it also hasn’t seen a refresh in the better part of a decade. But, because of the increasingly depressing state of the entire tech industry, Nvidia Shield TV Pro is getting a $100 price hike to $299, seven years after it first launched. more…
fullText:
The Nvidia Shield TV is an iconic piece of Android hardware but it also hasn’t seen a refresh in the better part of a decade. But, because of the increasingly depressing state of the entire tech industry, Nvidia Shield TV Pro is getting a $100 price hike to $299, seven years after it first launched.

Nvidia Shield TV Pro made its debut in October 2019 and, to this day, remains one of the most capable Android TV streamers on the market. While certain aspects haven’t aged perfectly, such as a lack of AV1 support and others, it remains unmatched in other places.

That’s a big part of the reason that, even so many years after it launched, Nvidia continues to produce the Shield TV.

But the $199 price point is gone. Effective today, Nvidia Shield TV Pro now costs $299.99. Nvidia attributed the price hike to the fact that “the cost of components, including memory, has increased substantially across the industry.” Alongside the change in price, Nvidia has also ended production of the base Shield TV that was also introduced in 2019. The “tube” Shield has been out of stock for months at this point, but Shield TV Pro was just restocked at Best Buy.

	

Shield TV Pro at Best Buy

Early this year, Nvidia said that it would continue software support for the Shield TV for the forseeable future. 

Shield isn’t the only streamer going up in price as a result of RAMageddon. Google TV Streamer saw a price hike to $149 recently, while other devices including Apple TV 4K and various Roku streamers also saw price hikes earlier this year. 

AI is just great, right?

title: Gemini 4 Is Here: When You May Be Able to Use Google’s New AI Model
snippet: Gemini 4 Argon is only available to cyber defenders now, a sign Google is gearing up for a wider launch soon.
fullText:
After months of delays, Google is gearing up to get back in the AI game. The company on Wednesday announced its newest frontier model, called Gemini 4 Argon. But you won’t be able to use it yet. Here’s why.

A lot has changed in the 10 months since Google released Gemini 3 — and crushed its competition. One is the introduction of the White House’s voluntary review process for new AI models, with which Google said in a blog post it is “actively engaged.” Another is the increasingly potent cybersecurity risk that new AI models pose for online companies, governments and consumers. Just take a look at all the AI agent hacks we’ve seen this summer.

Right now, Gemini 4 Argon is only available to specific cybersecurity defenders in Google’s Fairwind program. This has become the new way that AI companies roll out new frontier models: first to cybersecurity experts, who use it to shore up their own defenses and report any weaknesses, then to subscribers, and then eventually free users. OpenAI did this with GPT-6 Astra, same as Anthropic with Fable 5.

			

More from CNET

The slow-roll release is meant to give experts the time to find and patch issues before the AI is let loose on the internet. Past releases gave defenders a few weeks before the model was given a general release. Given that this is Google’s first model to go through this process, it could be a little bit longer. Google did not immediately respond to questions about the time frame of Gemini 4’s release.

Gemini 4: What we know so far

Gemini 4 Argon is the latest AI model from Google, capable of coding, multimodalities (like understanding images and charts) and reasoning. If it follows past releases, we can expect Gemini 4, or a version of it, to become the new model powering Google’s many, many AI features in Search, Docs and more. Google said that Gemini 4 Argon is particularly adept at business-related tasks, like software engineering, cybersecurity and knowledge work in legal and finance fields. Benchmarking data released by Google, comparing Gemini 4 to OpenAI’s Astra and Anthropic’s Fable 5.1, seems to back up those claims.

Google says it has been using Gemini 4 internally to help make the company more efficient, including in its quantum computing research and memory operations. It has a 1-million-token output limit. More tokens mean the AI can do more work and handle more complex tasks.

Google was rumored to release Gemini 3.5 Pro earlier this year, but reports say it held off to keep working on it. Even this week, there were concerns within the company that Gemini 4 wasn’t up to par on key tasks, such as coding, Bloomberg reports. We’ll have to wait until the model is released and put it to the test to see if those concerns were addressed before then.

				

					

						

													

					

					

						

Katelyn Chedraoui
						

						

							Reporter 2						
					

											

								

											Katelyn is a reporter with CNET covering artificial intelligence, including chatbots, image and video generators. Her work explores how new AI technology is infiltrating our lives, shaping the content we consume on social media and affecting the people behind the screens. She graduated from the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill with a degree in media and journalism. You can reach her at kchedraoui@cnet.com.

title: Google Home update rolling out with better ‘Find My Phone’ voice commands, smart home improvements
snippet: A new Google Home update has arrived with various improvements including better support for the “Find My Phone” voice command on Gemini speakers. more…
fullText:
A new Google Home update has arrived with various improvements including better support for the “Find My Phone” voice command on Gemini speakers.

In the Gemini for Home early access branch, Google says that users can expect “quality and reliability improvements” for the “Hey Google, find my phone” command that’s been around for years. It’s unclear exactly what’s changing, but this is a very useful voice command, so any upgrades will be welcome.

Improved Find My Phone reliability: Rolled out quality and reliability improvements to this fan-favorite feature when you ask Gemini to help locate your phone.

Other Gemini voice improvements in this latest update include filtering out background noise and voices, further speed/latency improvements, better support for multilingual households, and improved reliability to custom commands within Routines/automations.

In the Google Home app itself, there are quite a few updates to smart home functionality. This includes turning off lights when the brightness slider is dragged down to zero, improving camera and doorbell tiles, reducing Matter switches being incorrectly shown as offline, and improving setup for Nest devices.

	

Device Controller Enhancements

Accurate smart light shutoff: We’ve resolved an issue where sliding brightness down to 0% on single lights or group dimmers left bulbs powered on at minimum illumination instead of turning them off completely. Lowering your brightness to 0% now sends a definitive power-off command, preventing wasted energy and unexpected ambient glow.

Clearer online camera and doorbell tiles: Online cameras and doorbells now show as filled icons and accented tile colors at a glance, helping you instantly distinguish active cameras from idle ones.

Accurate offline switch status: We’ve resolved an issue where Matter switches failed to show their offline status or respond to taps on the All Devices tab, ensuring tiles properly render greyed out when disconnected.

Reliable Favorites tile gestures: We’ve resolved issues where long-pressing tiles in the Favorites tab failed to open device controllers or routine editors.

Smarter window covering detection: We’ve corrected device type resolution so awnings and curtains map accurately instead of defaulting all open-and-close window coverings to blinds.

Setup Improvements

Smoother smart device setup: We’ve delivered end-to-end reliability improvements when setting up Nest devices across iOS and Android. This includes under-the-hood fixes for Bluetooth connections and Wi-Fi pairing to eliminate common dropouts and stalls during the initial setup process.

Faster, standalone setup: When adding a new device to your home, the Google Home app can now securely cache network credentials on your mobile device, and reuse them for your next device.

There’s also a new preview option for Nest Doorbell ringtones.

The app update is rolling out now on Android, v4.31.27.1, while the Gemini updates are happening behind the scenes for those in early access.

title: Reddit is making two changes some long-time users won’t like
snippet: Reddit has announced two upcoming changes which are likely to prove unpopular with some long-time users. The company has already placed one restriction on Old Reddit, and it has now announced a second one. Additionally, RSS support is being discontinued … more…
fullText:
Reddit has announced two upcoming changes which are likely to prove unpopular with some long-time users.

The company has already placed one restriction on Old Reddit, and it has now announced a second one. Additionally, RSS support is being discontinued … 

Old Reddit

Reddit significantly changed its user interface way back in 2018, sparking significant objections from those who preferred the original version. To address this, the platform said that it would continue to provide access to what has become known as Old Reddit for as long as people kept using it.

The first change to this policy came in August of this year when the company required Old Reddit users to be logged in. It has now announced that the original UI will be limited to those who have used it within the last six months, denying access to new users.

In the next few months, we’ll further limit access for logged-in users to only those who have used Old Reddit in the last six months (which covers the vast majority of all Old Reddit users).

Reddit says that both moves were made to reduce AI scraping by companies (though this is apparently fine if they pay for the privilege).

The same rationale has been cited for discontinuing RSS feeds.

Because RSS is now a common surface for large-scale scraping and automated abuse, we’ll stop supporting RSS feeds on November 13, 2026.

This could be particularly problematic for subreddits who rely on these for moderation workflows. Reddit says it is aware of this and is recommending moderators use Devvit apps like Discord Relay.

Users unimpressed

Reading the comments in the thread, it’s clear that a lot of long-time users are very unhappy about the latest developments.

They said Old Reddit wasn’t going away, but Reddit lies all the time […] They’ll keep messing with stuff until they turn the site into a Twitter/Facebook hybrid and everyone except the Facebook/Twitter crowd abandons them.

What’s your take on the latest changes? Please share in the comments.

fullText:
Good morning and happy October. Today, I’m cringing at this gaggle of billionaires pretending to be human, vibing to the new Tinashe album, Popstar, and heartily dining on all the brutal ‘Digger’ reviews.

As a reminder, Inbox is the tech newsletter that goes beyond the news cycle. We cover the most important 9to5Google stories from the last couple of days along with a few highlights from around the web. We publish every Tuesday and Thursday, and if you like what you read, please subscribe.

Inbox is written by Daniel Bader. Read previous issues here, and then catch up with Ben Schoon’s excellent Weekender column published every Sunday.

⭐️ Starred

What year is it?

	

After months of waiting, Gemini 4 ‘Argon’ is finally out — sort of. Google unveiled the new state-of-the-art model late yesterday but has only made it available to “a set of trusted cyber defenders” while it undergoes testing. The company says it will get a wider release “as soon as possible.”

This is a big moment for Google. Many users and critics alike wrote it off completely, with one analysis firm saying “for all intents and purposes, we believe DeepMind is no longer a frontier lab.” While the company has released several useful, fast and affordable Flash-branded models in 2026, its latest salvo into state-of-the-art AI was back in November 2025 with Gemini 3 Pro. In fact, it was so good that for a brief time Google was considered to be well ahead of OpenAI and Anthropic, and presaged a “code red” inside the frontier labs.

It’s hard to overstate how important it is for Gemini 4 to succeed. After a massive executive shuffle in August saw Demis Hassabis and Jeff Dean removed from the core management team, most of DeepMind’s operations were shifted from London to Mountain View, where new head Koray Kavukcuoglu reports directly to Google CEO Sundar Pichai.

While there has been speculation that Google, with its entrenched customer base, would walk away from the frontier in favor of cheaper, more product-focused pursuits, Kavukcuoglu has refuted those rumors. Earlier this month, he said, “To put it very bluntly, there’s nothing other than being at the frontier that is important for us. We have the whole full stack… and we are able to optimize to be able to achieve our goals.”

According to benchmarks, Gemini 4 is competitive with GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5 in most tests, and is trained to be much better at agentic tasks than any previous Gemini model. It’s also better aligned, with a focus on cybersecurity, and has a massive 1M token output limit, which makes it far more capable of producing large bodies of work in one prompt with less compaction.

The big question, though, is whether Argon will be competitive in the real world. A Bloomberg report published shortly before the embargo lifted on the Gemini 4 news quoted anonymous Google employees skeptical of its coding abilities. From Bloomberg: “While Gemini 4 has performed well on benchmarks widely used to gauge model efficacy, it does less well when employees actually put it to work, according to people with direct access to the effort. The model struggles to handle certain coding tasks, said the people, who requested anonymity to discuss an internal matter.”

Argon is also curiously priced. Its introductory rate of $2/$10 per million input/output tokens matches OpenAI’s Sol 6.1 cost right now, but will eventually double to hit the $4/$20 price of Claude Opus 5.5. While still significantly cheaper than Astra or Fable, it has to prove its mettle with users before Google is welcomed back into the arms of the fickle AI masses.

Android Central, the blog I worked at from 2016 through 2021, was shut down yesterday by Future, the company that bought it in 2020 alongside iMore and Windows Central. iMore was already shut down and turned into…something AI slop-related, and I guess it was AC’s turn to be culled.

I made friends there that I still treasure today, and was privileged to hire and train a number of incredible writers and editors who spent many years doing wonderful work. title: Google Play adding Usage-Based Billing subscriptions aimed at AI apps
snippet: Google Play today is giving Android developers more payment options around subscriptions, including Usage-Based Billing. more…
fullText:
Google Play today is giving Android developers more payment options around subscriptions, including Usage-Based Billing.

Google says the “subscription landscape is evolving rapidly” due to generative AI and “increasingly sophisticated app experiences.” 

End users should be on the lookout for Usage-Based Billing to support generative AI apps and other usage-based services. This “prepaid metered billing” works by letting users “automatically top up their balance whenever it falls below a set threshold.” 

For large groups like businesses and schools, there’s Multi-Quantity Subscription Purchase. Organizations can “make multiple subscription purchases in a single transaction and easily assign those as seats or subscriptions to team members or students.”

	

Mixed Carts allow developers to sell auto-renewing subscriptions and one-time products at the same time. For example:

This unified experience also opens up powerful upsell opportunities for your business—such as offering targeted discounts if an end user purchases a complete bundle of a subscription and complementary in-app items together.

Cross-Developer Bundling lets developers “create and sell a hard bundle of two or more complementary subscriptions in your own catalog.” The example Google gives is bundling a language-learning app with a travel guide service for a “combined subscription at a discounted rate.”

This capability allows you to team up with other developers—or combine offerings across your own portfolio of apps—to deliver massive value through a single purchase.

These Play Store features are “currently available or rolling out through [Google’s] Early Access Program.”

title: Google stands by Gemini 4 performance as some claim it ‘struggles’ in real-world use
snippet: Google yesterday unveiled its new flagship Gemini 4 model with some impressive scores, but a report suggests that it might “struggle” in some cases. more…
fullText:
Google yesterday unveiled its new flagship Gemini 4 model with some impressive scores, but a report suggests that it might “struggle” in some cases.

Google announces Gemini 4 Argon as its new frontier model

Bloomberg reports that, internally, Google employees have found that Gemini 4’s real-world performance doesn’t always line up with its benchmark scores. During the unveiling of Gemini 4 Argon, Google showed that its new model outpaced competitors including OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra in many key areas.

The report cites Googlers who found that the model “does less well when employees actually put it to work,” and that it “struggles to handle certain coding tasks.” Google, speaking to Bloomberg on the claims, said that it “would be inaccurate to say that Gemini 4 is underperforming in areas such as coding,” also referencing comments from Koray Kavukcuoglu, the head of Google DeepMind, from late September, when he said that “it’s a certainty that we are always gonna be at the frontier.” The report cites one Googler who said that there’s a “large consensus” that Gemini 4 is at the frontier amongst employees, while others are concerned that Gemini “will still lag behind” competing models from Anthropic and OpenAI. Clearly, there’s a split in how employees view the model’s performance.

Gemini 4 Argon brings welcome upgrades to the model, including an expanded output limit of up to 1 million tokens, while Google also explained that the model is “highly capable at cybersecurity defense” and shows “leading performance” in other use cases. Gemini 4 Argon comes at a cost of “$4 per 1M input tokens and $20 per 1M output tokens” but will see introductory pricing which is half of that.

title: iFixit teardown of the new AirPods 5 reveals first real repairability improvement
snippet: iFixit’s teardown of the new AirPods 5 is now up, revealing an important, albeit tiny, repairability improvement. Watch it below. more…
fullText:
iFixit’s teardown of the new AirPods 5 is now up, revealing an important, albeit tiny, repairability improvement. Watch it below.

Record repairability score at 2/10

Since Apple launched the original AirPods in 2016, iFixit has consistently given them a 0 out of 10 for repairability. From heavily glued-in batteries and soldered connections to housings that are nearly impossible to open and reassemble without damage, AirPods have always been notoriously difficult to repair.

With the new AirPods 5, however, iFixit says Apple has taken a tiny step in the right direction, provided the repair is being done by a skilled professional or particularly adventurous DIY enthusiast.

In their new teardown video, iFixit shows that the batteries inside each earbud can be removed and replaced without necessarily destroying the AirPods in the process, which has led them to give AirPods a repairability score above zero for the first time.

Granted, the new AirPods 5 only scored 2 out of 10, but that’s still two points more than every previous generation combined.

iFixit notes that the left and right batteries are not interchangeable, as they use reversed polarity and slightly different contact placement.

That said, this is basically the long and short of AirPods 5 repairability. As iFixit shows in the video, going any further into the earbuds is still impossible without destroying them, and the same is true of their charging case.

iFixit’s teardown also includes its always-fascinating CT scans, which offer a detailed look at just how densely Apple has packed the batteries, MEMS microphones, H2 chip, and other tiny components inside each earbud.

fullText:

What’s new in Android 17 on Samsung Galaxy?

One UI 9, Samsung’s Android 17 update, continues the trend of evolution more than overhaul. The update introduces some slight design tweaks, more AI-powered features, and other changes built on the redesign that debuted in One UI 7 and was iterated in last year’s Android 16-based One UI 8. 

Some key changes in One UI 9 include:

Warranty & Samsung Care status in the Settings menu

Broader support for Now Nudge

My FanCam automatic video cropping based on a select subject

More Quick Panel (quick settings) customization

AI privacy alerts

Upgrades to Samsung DeX

New lock screen clocks that can adapt to your wallpaper

Samsung Galaxy devices with Android 17 – The full list

While Samsung hasn’t confirmed an exact schedule for its One UI 9 and Android 17 rollout for Galaxy devices, there are updates now rolling out in parts of the globe. Below you’ll find a regularly-updated list of every Samsung Galaxy device that has received a stable Android 17 update so far.

Galaxy S26

Galaxy S26+

Galaxy S26 Ultra

Galaxy S25 (limited availability)

One UI 9 changelog

Here’s the full changelog from Samsung for One UI 9, as listed for the Galaxy S26 series. Some features may vary by device.

Galaxy AI

Enhanced Now nudge

Now nudge provides helpful suggestions in more places throughout your Galaxy experience. In addition to the keyboard, suggestions will now appear in conversation notifications and in a floating button in the bottom right corner of the screen. There are also several new types of suggestions, like entering reservation details or addresses and saving places in Google Maps.

Focus on someone important

My FanCam lets you select a person in a video and follow them automatically while cropping out the rest of the video.

Interpreter keeps your conversation in front of you

In conversation mode, you can scroll through the whole conversation while you’re still talking.

See useful information during calls

See relevant events and other information related to your current call on the call screen.

Productivity and multitasking

More customizable quick panel

You can now rearrange and customize the controls in your quick panel even more than before. You can change the size of the brightness and volume sliders as well as the media player. You can also separate the sound mode button from the volume slider.

Privacy, security, and device protection

Warranty and care

The new Warranty and care menu in settings lets you check your warranty information and access diagnostic checks and useful information for keeping your Galaxy in top condition.

Lock down your phone quickly

It’s now easier to securely lock your phone in a hurry. Just press and hold the Volume down and Side buttons at the same time or tap the Power button in the quick panel. This prevents biometrics from being used the next time you unlock your phone.

Location access transparency

Stay on top of your location privacy. A blue indicator will appear at the top of the screen when an app accesses your location. Tap the indicator in the quick panel to see which app it is.

Stronger security and privacy protection

Alerts will appear in your Now brief to let you know about risks from malware, apps from unknown sources, unnecessary permissions, and other issues that may put your security and privacy at risk. Apps that have been identified as malicious or vulnerable will be blocked from opening until you make a decision about whether to remove them.

AI privacy alerts

Get help protecting your personal data. AI will monitor how apps use permissions and notify you about unnecessary access to your personal data.

Samsung Health

New look for Samsung Health

Samsung Health has been redesigned to make your health data easier to understand. Enjoy clearer visuals, improved charts, and a more engaging experience to help you reach your health goals.

Customize your Health home screen

Resize cards and organize them by category, like Activity, Sleep, Mindfulness, and Nutrition, so your top priorities are easy to access.

Log health data quickly

It’s now easier to add your health information right from the Samsung Health home screen. You can log your mood, meals, and more. You can even use the camera for faster input.

Advanced trend analysis

Track your progress with improved trend charts in Samsung Health. View data in hourly, daily, or weekly intervals, pinch to zoom in for a closer look, and overlay multiple charts to compare your performance across different periods.

Monitor changes in your sleep vitals

Samsung Health helps you notice meaningful changes in your sleep health data. Use Galaxy Watch or Ring measurements to better understand your daily health patterns.

Manage your heart health

Track key health metrics and lifestyle factors that affect your heart. A daily score based on your sleep, exercise, BMI, and blood pressure helps you better understand your current heart health trends.

Track your cardio load

See how your workouts and activity impact your heart so you’ll know when to push harder and when to rest. Your target cardio load range adjusts daily based on your recent activity and training focus.

Check your fitness index

Your Fitness Index is an overall score calculated using five key fitness metrics: body composition, cardio, strength, flexibility, and endurance. Set a goal and unlock personalized insights tailored to your results.

Keep your ears safe

The new Hearing tracker monitors sound levels detected by your Galaxy Watch and headphone audio levels to help you manage your exposure to loud sounds.

View your cycle and body rhythm

Get a more personalized view of your cycle and body rhythm with new cycle tracking options. You can view your cycle information in your calendar and better understand your health patterns.

Bixby

Activate Bixby with a gesture

Talk to Bixby just by raising your phone close to your mouth and speaking. No wake-up word needed.

Manage your conversations

Keep your chats organized. Search them, rename them, or pin your favorites. You can also delete all of your past conversations at once.

Bixby on the Home screen

Add a Bixby widget to type or talk to Bixby or jump directly to your conversation history.

Accessibility

Discover new Accessibility features

Check the What’s new menu in Accessibility settings to learn about and try the latest Accessibility features for your Galaxy.

Text spotlight for easier reading

Need a closer look? Tap any text on the screen to show it enlarged and highlighted in its own window. You can also customize the font size, colors, and other settings to match your preferences.

Physical keyboard shortcuts

Use shortcuts on your physical keyboard to access the Accessibility settings you need without touching the screen.

Mouse keys enhancements

New options are available when using your keyboard for mouse interactions including speed and acceleration control. You can also use the keyboard’s number pad to point and click.

Replace swipe with single tap

The Replace swipe with single tap option is now located in the Dexterity and interaction menu instead of the Assistant menu for easier access.

Select to speak

Get quick audio readouts without turning on full TalkBack. With the new Select to speak feature, you can select an item on your screen, like text or an image, and hear it read or described out loud.

Improved TalkBack updates

TalkBack updates can now be applied with a simple app update from the Play Store, helping you get the latest accessibility features and enhancements.

Even more improvements

New Lock screen clock

The default clock on your Lock screen has been redesigned with a cleaner and more modern look that adapts to match your wallpaper.

Samsung DeX enhancements

It’s easier to move an app window from one desktop to another using the menu at the top of the window. Desktop previews are now available at the top of the Recents screen, making it easier to switch with a single tap.
