Anbernic’s $69.99 RG34XX is still cheaper than the Pocket Advance and may seem like a better alternative, but I think Ayaneo’s is absolutely worth the extra $40. It’s a more powerful and capable handheld with a higher-res display, and I much prefer the Pocket Advance’s larger D-pad and shoulder button arrangement. I also find the quality of Anbernic’s hardware to be hit and miss. Similar to what others have reported on Reddit, I’ve experienced intermittent issues with the responsiveness of the RG34XX’s D-pad. I haven’t had the motivation to crack it open to attempt a DIY fix, and with the Pocket Advance now in my collection, it’s doubtful I ever will.

Even with buttons that feel very soft, the Pocket Advance is easily the best GBA clone currently available.

The Pocket Advance is one of the best retro handhelds currently available and not just because of its nostalgic retro design. As long as you temper your gaming expectations and won’t be frustrated by what it can’t play, it’s an excellent way to revisit and enjoy games from Nintendo’s earlier handheld era.

title: Pixel Watch 4 & 5’s handy USB-C travel charger is currently on sale
snippet: Launched earlier this year, that useful little USB-C charger dongle for Google’s Pixel Watch 4 and Pixel Watch 5 smartwatches is currently discounted. more…
fullText:
Launched earlier this year, that useful little USB-C charger dongle for Google’s Pixel Watch 4 and Pixel Watch 5 smartwatches is currently discounted.

Google’s latest take on smartwatch charging debuted on last year’s Pixel Watch 4 series, with two pins popping out of the smartwatch to connect with a magnetic dock. Google’s official charging cable works well enough, but it’s just another thing to plug in when you’re traveling. 

Wasserstein, a long-time Made for Google accessory partner, launched a handy alternative earlier this year. A simple charger that attaches to the end of any USB-C cable give you the option to cut down on some bulk while still being able to easily top off your smartwatch on the go. Its price was in flux for quite a while, but eventually settled at $30.

Right now, though, it’s discounted to $25. Not a huge discount, but it certainly makes the handy charger an easier buy if you have any travel coming up through the end of the year.

	

Wasserstein USB-C charger for Pixel Watch 4 & 5 at Amazon

As a reminder, this works with all Pixel Watch 4 and Pixel Watch 5 smartwatches, regardless of if you’re using the 41mm or 45mm sizes. You’ll want to plug into at least 7.5W of power, but you’re likely getting that from whatever charger you’re using with your smartphone anyway. Just keep in mind that Pixel Watch 3 and prior cannot use this charger.

title: Apple releases macOS 27.0.1 Golden Gate, plus macOS Tahoe 26.7.1 and macOS Sequoia 15.8.1 [U]
snippet: Following two release candidates, Apple today released macOS Tahoe 26.7.1 and macOS Sequoia 15.8.1, as well as macOS 27.0.1. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Following two release candidates, Apple today released macOS Tahoe 26.7.1 and macOS Sequoia 15.8.1, as well as macOS 27.0.1. Here are the details.

macOS 27.0.1, macOS 26.7.1 and macOS 15.8.1 now available

After two release candidates, Apple is now rolling out macOS Tahoe 26.7.1 and macOS Sequoia 15.8.1, in addition to macOS 27.0.1 Golden Gate, the first update since the release of macOS 27 earlier this month.

Today’s releases come exactly one week after Apple rolled out the second round of release candidates, which also included public releases the following day.

Apple’s release notes during the RC mentioned only standard security fixes and performance improvements, but recent point releases have included significant security patches, many of which address vulnerabilities discovered with the help of AI tools.

Apple has even confirmed that the growing capabilities of AI tools are affecting its security release cadence. In June, the company said it had pushed out fixes originally planned for version 26.6 ahead of schedule because AI can speed up the development of malicious hacking tools, reducing the amount of time Apple wants to leave between making fixes public and getting them into users’ hands.

Apple will likely release the security details for macOS 27.0.1 Golden Gate, macOS Tahoe 26.7.1, and macOS Sequoia 15.8.1 in the coming hours, and we’ll report back with the noteworthy tidbits.

Update, 1:59 p.m. ET: Apple says macOS 27.0.1 Golden Gate “has no published CVE entries,” but says macOS Tahoe 26.7.1 and macOS Sequoia 15.8.1 fix the following issue:

CoreGraphics

Available for: macOS Sequoia

Impact: Processing a maliciously crafted file may lead to arbitrary code execution. Apple is aware of a report that this issue may have been exploited in an extremely sophisticated attack against specific targeted individuals on versions of iOS before iOS 27.

Description: An out-of-bounds write issue was addressed with improved bounds checking.

CVE-2026-86950: Meta Product Security

The release build for today’s macOS releases are:

macOS Sequoia 15.8: 24H32

macOS Tahoe 26.7.1: 25G241

macOS 27.0.1 Golden Gate: 26A5434

title: Anthropic upgrades Claude with new Sonnet 5.5 model, details here
snippet: Anthropic is upgrading Claude Sonnet, replacing Sonnet 5 from June with Sonnet 5.5 as the best medium-sized model. more…
fullText:
Anthropic is upgrading Claude Sonnet, replacing Sonnet 5 from June with Sonnet 5.5 as the best medium-sized model.

Claude Sonnet 5.5 upgrades Anthropic’s medium model

Anthropic currently offers a few AI models under the Claude umbrella. 

The three main models are Haiku (smallest and cheapest), Sonnet (medium size and price), and Opus (largest and most expensive of the three).

There’s also Fable/Mythos, which is even more capable and costly, which represents Anthropic’s highest tier.

Today’s new Claude model follows the arrival of Opus 5.5 last week. Anthropic promised to upgrade Sonnet and Haiku “in the coming weeks” at the time.

Introducing Claude Sonnet 5.5, the second model in the Claude 5.5 family.

It’s a clear upgrade over Sonnet 5, runs more than 30% faster, and costs up to 30% less for most work. pic.twitter.com/UvXD8mDTF1

— Claude (@claudeai) September 28, 2026

Anthropic says Sonnet 5.5 is strongest at everyday tasks with a clear scope, including fixing bugs and creating polished documents, slides, and spreadsheets.

The company also highlights its design capabilities, from refining user interfaces to producing slides that follow templates and need minimal editing.

Early testers described it as a better collaborator than Sonnet 5, Anthropic says, with clearer writing and speed suited to quick iteration on less complex tasks.

Sonnet 5.5 keeps Sonnet 5’s pricing: $2 per million input tokens, $10 per million output tokens, and $0.20 per million cache reads.

Anthropic says it typically uses far fewer tokens to complete the same work, while generating output more than 30% faster than Sonnet 5, making it the fastest Sonnet model to date.

With cybersecurity capabilities comparable to Opus 5, Sonnet 5.5 is the first Sonnet model to launch with cyber safeguards and fallbacks similar to those used for Anthropic’s most capable models.

Its biology safeguards remain unchanged from Sonnet 5. Anthropic says both target a narrow set of high-risk requests, leaving routine software development and most life sciences work unaffected.

title: Slovenia’s .si domain sees a surge in registrations after Trump’s ‘super intelligence’ order
snippet: The .si domain name is seeing unprecedented demand after President Trump's super intelligence executive order.
fullText:
In not-so-surprising news, the .si domain name is seeing unprecedented demand after President Trump signed an executive order mandating all government agencies to refer to “AI” and “artificial intelligence” as “SI” and “super intelligence.” It echoes what happened at the start of the AI boom, when interest in the .ai domain name—associated with the country Anguilla—spiked and brought in millions for the island territory. 

Now it’s .si’s turn in the spotlight. The domain name was commonly associated with Slovenia, where, ironically, First Lady Melania Trump is from. Klara Herman, a spokesperson at Registry SI, the official organization that manages Slovenia’s domains, told the BBC earlier this week that there was a 2,199% increase in .si domain name purchases in September. However, she was cautious about linking the boost only to President Trump. 

Still, the Registry noted 11,000 new addresses recorded on September 30th, the day after President Trump signed the executive order, and almost 13,000 new .si domain names were registered in the past 24 hours. 

We reached out to a few other web hosting sites to see if they had seen similar trends. GoDaddy said they don’t yet host the .si domain, and Squarespace hadn’t yet responded as of the time of publication. Wix, interestingly enough, said that they weren’t seeing any “meaningful uptick” on their end, and that it’s been minimal on the site since September 29th. “It’s still early so that could change,” a Wix spokesperson said. 

But web hosting platform Hostinger told me that .si is now its second most popular domain extension, right after .com. It found that among its customers, almost 4,300 registered .si on September 30th and about 5,400 on October 1st; more than three-quarters of all .si domains registered since September 23 came in the last two days. It found that more than half the buyers were coming from the U.S. and India. 

Curiously enough, on Hostinger, only around 3% of the .si domains are explicitly related to AI, it said. Most are “unclassified,” — meaning their names don’t match any specific category. It said that most of those registering the .si domain name seem to be people and businesses, though there is a speculative element, in that people could be buying the domains to resell them later. 

Upon hearing this, my first thought went back to what a founder messaged me earlier this week, noting that .si domains were reselling for over a million dollars. Kim Than, CEO of Genius PR, who specializes in working with AI and crypto founders, told me that he already bought the .si version of his company name “to protect the brand in case this takes off like .ai.” And did so because it was cheap, so he figured he might as well “secure it now than potentially pay a lot more later.”

Than sees domain names as digital collectibles and wants to pick up a few more while the price is still good, and he might resell them later; one can also tokenize domains, he said, and trade them on the blockchain, though he’s not sure if .si is supported just yet. “A few founder friends are buying too cause we think it’s the new AI boom,” he continued. “Who knows how far it goes, but I’m happy to take a bet.”  

There is a chance that .si could become pretty popular. President Trump’s executive order said that “the capabilities of today’s frontier systems do much more than imitate or automate discrete aspects of human intelligence,” and that they “increasingly represent not merely artificial intelligence but a new super intelligence.” 

Klaudijus Januitis, head of domains at Hostinger, told me that he expects the demand for .si to keep growing, though he doesn’t see that domain as replacing .ai anytime soon. Instead, as noted by that founder and his friends, Januitis said .si is right now a more available and a “more affordable second option.” 

“Slovenia will not see what Anguilla saw,” he said, noting that, for one, Anguilla charges a “premium” to use .si and that money goes straight to the government, while .si is a fraction of the cost and goes to the registry rather than the treasury. For example, on Hostinger, .si costs around $12 dollars a year while .ai goes for $90 and requires a two-year commitment. “For Anguilla, .ai became a second economy. For Slovenia, .si is a nice bonus.”

However, she was cautious about linking the boost only to President Trump.

title: TechCrunch Disrupt 2026: Clay’s Kareem Amin on the rise of the GTM engineer
snippet: Clay Co-founder and CEO Kareem Amin joins the AI Stage to discuss the rise of GTM engineer at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026. Register for your ticket and get a second pass at 50% off.
fullText:
Two years ago, most companies didn’t have a GTM engineer. Now the role is showing up across tech, with practitioners using AI and automation to build revenue systems that once required multiple people, tools, and manual processes.

What changed — and what does it mean for the way companies find customers and grow?

At TechCrunch Disrupt 2026, Clay co-founder and CEO Kareem Amin will take the AI Stage for “The GTM Engineer: How AI Created Tech’s Next Big Job Category.” He’ll trace how AI has changed the traditional go-to-market stack and helped create a new discipline in its place, giving attendees a look at what AI-native GTM looks like in practice and how it’s changing company growth.

Image Credits:TechCrunch

AI is giving go-to-market teams new ways to research prospects, work with data, personalize outreach, and automate workflows that once moved between separate tools and teams. As those capabilities converge, companies are rethinking not only their GTM technology, but who builds and manages the systems behind growth.

If you’re building a company or rethinking how your team approaches sales, marketing, and growth, this is a new role worth understanding. Secure your Disrupt pass and see where GTM engineering fits into the next generation of go-to-market. Get a second pass at a 50% discount, and more savings for groups of four or more.

What does a GTM engineer actually do?

Traditional go-to-market work can involve hours of researching accounts, cleaning data, qualifying leads, preparing outreach, and moving information between systems. GTM engineering uses AI, data, and automation to turn more of that work into repeatable systems.

Clay coined the role in 2023. Its own GTM engineering guide describes GTM engineers as practitioners who build automated revenue workflows rather than executing individual GTM tasks by hand. The company says roughly 100 GTM engineering job listings are now appearing each month, including roles at companies such as Cursor, Lovable, and Webflow.

For founders and GTM leaders deciding where to put their next dollar or whether to make their next hire, this session offers another way to think about growth. Do you add more people to execute the existing process, or build systems that let the people you already have execute differently?

At Disrupt, Amin will put the shift into context and explore what AI-native GTM looks like in practice. Get your ticket to Disrupt to understand a role that barely existed a few years ago but could change how your next sales, marketing, or growth team operates.

Clay puts AI to work across the GTM stack

Clay started in Brooklyn in 2017 with a goal: give more people access to the power of programming. Its original spreadsheet let users connect information and automate work without writing code. When salespeople, growth teams, and agencies began using it to find and reach customers, Clay followed them into go-to-market.

Today, the company provides infrastructure for GTM teams to access data, run agentic workflows and launch campaigns. Its OpenAI-powered agent, Claygent, automates research and outreach for sales, marketing and recruiting teams.

That evolution has been accompanied by rapid growth. TechCrunch reported in February that the company had tripled annual recurring revenue to $100 million in a year and announced an employee tender offer at a $5 billion valuation. Clay has continued growing since then, announcing a $115 million Series D in September at a $7.1 billion valuation.

Clay is also investing directly in the job category at the center of Amin’s Disrupt session, announcing a $1 million scholarship fund in September to train GTM engineers.

For companies trying to determine where AI can make a meaningful difference in revenue operations, add Amin’s session to your Disrupt agenda and see how one company is putting that model into practice.

From product leader to a new GTM approach

Kareem Amin co-founded Clay in 2017 and serves as its co-founder and CEO. Before Clay, he was VP of product at The Wall Street Journal and co-founded collaboration startup Frame, which Sailthru acquired in 2012.

Amin started Clay around the idea of putting programming capabilities into more people’s hands. AI eventually gave that idea a new application: enabling GTM teams to build systems that automate research, data enrichment, and outreach without relying on traditional engineering resources for every workflow.

Want to understand what a GTM engineer could mean for your own growth strategy? Secure your Disrupt pass and hear directly from one of the founders helping define the category.

See what AI-native GTM looks like in practice at Disrupt

“The GTM Engineer: How AI Created Tech’s Next Big Job Category” is one of 200+ sessions across six industry stages, roundtables, and breakouts at Disrupt, October 13–15 at Moscone West in San Francisco. More than 10,000 founders, investors, operators, and tech leaders are expected, along with 250+ speakers and 300+ exhibiting startups.

Beyond the sessions, matchmaking, dealmaking, and networking give attendees opportunities to meet potential customers, investors, partners, and other founders confronting many of the same growth challenges.

GTM engineering may be a new job category, but the problem it addresses isn’t: how do you find and reach the right customers without simply adding more people and more tools? At Disrupt, you can see how AI is changing that equation — and meet the people building what comes next.

title: iOS 27 breaks 15 years of muscle memory on iPhone and iPad
snippet: Since iOS 5 in 2011, the iPhone and iPad have included Notification Center, a central place to find alerts from various apps in chronological order. Starting with iOS 27, Apple is making a major change to how users open Notification Center on iPhone and iPad. iOS 27 is here after a summer of beta releases. The behavior changed slightly between the first two releases. However, this change shipped, and I’m still adjusting to it. more…
fullText:
Since iOS 5 in 2011, the iPhone and iPad have included Notification Center, a central place to find alerts from various apps in chronological order.

Starting with iOS 27, Apple is making a major change to how users open Notification Center on iPhone and iPad.

iOS 27 is here after a summer of beta releases. The behavior changed slightly between the first two releases. However, this change shipped, and I’m still adjusting to it.

Siri AI takes over the swipe gesture for a lot of the iPhone and iPad top edge

Opening Notification Center is unchanged on iOS 27 and iPadOS 27 by default. However, enabling Siri AI changes a key swipe gesture on both iPhone and iPad.

One of the many ways of invoking Siri AI, once enabled, is by swiping down from the center of the top edge of your iPhone or iPad display. This previously opened Notification Center.

You can still access Notification Center by swiping down from the top-left corner once Siri AI is enabled. Alerts now animate in from the top left corner. This is a way to point users toward Notification Center’s smaller surface area.

Apple is greatly prioritizing Siri AI access in iOS 27. The majority of the top edge is devoted to invoking the new Siri experience.

The last time Apple made a change to accessing Notification Center came when Control Center moved from a swipe up gesture from the bottom to a top-right corner swipe down gesture on iPhone X. Apple later unified this experience across devices.

Notifications now live in the top left corner

Now it’s Notification Center’s turn to be put in the corner. On iPadOS 27 beta 1 in particular, the area above Home screen app icons was pretty much devoted to invoking Siri AI. The area for opening Notification Center actually shrank if you disable displaying AM/PM or the date.

	

Apple improved this with iPadOS 27 beta 2, creating a more uniform region on either side. It’s roughly the size of two app columns with Notification Center on the left and Control Center on the right. The rest is for invoking Siri. 

After 15 years of muscle memory, it’ll take some time to determine if this change is worth it or something that should be reconsidered. In the meantime, early feedback sounds overwhelmingly positive around Apple’s new Siri AI system. Hearing that Siri is good now will also take some getting used to, I’m sure.

After months of using the new behavior, I’m certain I’d toggle it off if there were a setting to do so. Since there’s no option to disable invoking Siri from the top middle swipe down, the only thing to do is build new muscle memory around avoiding the center.

What do you think? Would you change this back if you could? Is accessing Siri from the swipe-down gesture worth the change? Share your thoughts in the comments.

title: This fake Mac Zoom installer has a sneaky way to bypass Gatekeeper
snippet: Cybersecurity company Jamf has discovered a fake Mac installer for the videoconferencing app Zoom that uses a sneaky way to bypass Apple’s Gatekeeper protection against malware. The malware does actually install Zoom, but also an infostealer that captures data and sends it to the attacker’s server … more…
fullText:
Cybersecurity company Jamf has discovered a fake Mac installer for the videoconferencing app Zoom that uses a sneaky way to bypass Apple’s Gatekeeper protection against malware.

The malware does actually install Zoom, but also an infostealer that captures data and sends it to the attacker’s server …

Normally, when you try to install a Mac app that Apple hasn’t notarized, macOS will refuse to open it. There is a workaround to allow you to do so, but it’s somewhat fiddly, and attackers have to find some way to persuade users to do it.

The criminals behind the malware Jamf has dubbed CloudSyncD have found a clever way to make this seem more normal to users. The app installer dropper includes a background image with instructions, as shown above.

CloudSyncD arrives as a disk image that mounts as a volume named Zoom, laid out to look like any ordinary Mac installer: an application icon on the left, an alias to Applications on the right. The difference is the background image, which carries a numbered Setup list telling the victim to open System Settings, go to Privacy & Security, scroll to the Security section, click Open Anyway, and enter their administrator password. Those are instructions to bypass Gatekeeper.

You kind of have to admire the creativity of this.

Once the malware is installed, it can record user-entered data and send it to the attackers as frequently as every eight seconds.

As always, you should only ever install Mac apps from the official Mac App Store or the websites of developers you trust.

title: Samsung rolling out Android 17, One UI 9 for more Galaxy S26 users – here’s everything new
snippet: After a lengthy delay, Samsung is finally rolling out its Android 17-based One UI 9 update for Galaxy S26 users in the US more broadly. more…
fullText:
After a lengthy delay, Samsung is finally rolling out its Android 17-based One UI 9 update for Galaxy S26 users in the US more broadly.

Samsung announced its One UI 9 rollout early this month, but updates didn’t start flowing. Last week the update finally started to trickle out in the US, but only for users on T-Mobile. 

Now, the floodgates are starting to crack. 

Galaxy S26 users on unlocked devices in the US are now seeing One UI 9 land, Android 17 in tow, at least for those who were enrolled in the beta program. It’s still not a full rollout, but it’s another step towards the full debut. SammyGuru and others spotted the rollout which, for those in the beta, measures around 650MB, while Android Authority also cites some Samsung changelogs that detail everything new.

	

Samsung’s official changelog follows (edited for formatting):

One UI 9

Galaxy AI

Enhanced Now nudge

Now nudge provides helpful suggestions in more places throughout your Galaxy experience. In addition to the keyboard, suggestions will now appear in conversation notifications and in a floating button in the bottom right corner of the screen. There are also several new types of suggestions, like entering reservation details or addresses and saving places in Google Maps.

Focus on someone important

My FanCam lets you select a person in a video and follow them automatically while cropping out the rest of the video.

Interpreter keeps your conversation in front of you

In conversation mode, you can scroll through the whole conversation while you’re still talking.

See useful information during calls

See relevant events and other information related to your current call on the call screen.

Productivity and multitasking

More customizable quick panel

You can now rearrange and customize the controls in your quick panel even more than before. You can change the size of the brightness and volume sliders as well as the media player. You can also separate the sound mode button from the volume slider.

Privacy, security, and device protection

Warranty and care

The new Warranty and care menu in settings lets you check your warranty information and access diagnostic checks and useful information for keeping your Galaxy in top condition.

Lock down your phone quickly

It’s now easier to securely lock your phone in a hurry. Just press and hold the Volume down and Side buttons at the same time or tap the Power button in the quick panel. This prevents biometrics from being used the next time you unlock your phone.

Location access transparency

Stay on top of your location privacy. A blue indicator will appear at the top of the screen when an app accesses your location. Tap the indicator in the quick panel to see which app it is.

Stronger security and privacy protection

Alerts will appear in your Now brief to let you know about risks from malware, apps from unknown sources, unnecessary permissions, and other issues that may put your security and privacy at risk. Apps that have been identified as malicious or vulnerable will be blocked from opening until you make a decision about whether to remove them.

AI privacy alerts

Get help protecting your personal data. AI will monitor how apps use permissions and notify you about unnecessary access to your personal data.

Samsung Health

New look for Samsung Health

Samsung Health has been redesigned to make your health data easier to understand. Enjoy clearer visuals, improved charts, and a more engaging experience to help you reach your health goals.

Customize your Health home screen

Resize cards and organize them by category, like Activity, Sleep, Mindfulness, and Nutrition, so your top priorities are easy to access.

Log health data quickly

It’s now easier to add your health information right from the Samsung Health home screen. You can log your mood, meals, and more. You can even use the camera for faster input.

Advanced trend analysis

Track your progress with improved trend charts in Samsung Health. View data in hourly, daily, or weekly intervals, pinch to zoom in for a closer look, and overlay multiple charts to compare your performance across different periods.

Monitor changes in your sleep vitals

Samsung Health helps you notice meaningful changes in your sleep health data. Use Galaxy Watch or Ring measurements to better understand your daily health patterns.

Manage your heart health

Track key health metrics and lifestyle factors that affect your heart. A daily score based on your sleep, exercise, BMI, and blood pressure helps you better understand your current heart health trends.

Track your cardio load

See how your workouts and activity impact your heart so you’ll know when to push harder and when to rest. Your target cardio load range adjusts daily based on your recent activity and training focus.

Check your fitness index

Your Fitness Index is an overall score calculated using five key fitness metrics: body composition, cardio, strength, flexibility, and endurance. Set a goal and unlock personalized insights tailored to your results.

Keep your ears safe

The new Hearing tracker monitors sound levels detected by your Galaxy Watch and headphone audio levels to help you manage your exposure to loud sounds.

View your cycle and body rhythm

Get a more personalized view of your cycle and body rhythm with new cycle tracking options. You can view your cycle information in your calendar and better understand your health patterns.

Bixby

Activate Bixby with a gesture

Talk to Bixby just by raising your phone close to your mouth and speaking. No wake-up word needed.

Manage your conversations

Keep your chats organized. Search them, rename them, or pin your favorites. You can also delete all of your past conversations at once.

Bixby on the Home screen

Add a Bixby widget to type or talk to Bixby or jump directly to your conversation history.

Accessibility

Discover new Accessibility features

Check the What’s new menu in Accessibility settings to learn about and try the latest Accessibility features for your Galaxy.

Text spotlight for easier reading

Need a closer look? Tap any text on the screen to show it enlarged and highlighted in its own window. You can also customize the font size, colors, and other settings to match your preferences.

Physical keyboard shortcuts

Use shortcuts on your physical keyboard to access the Accessibility settings you need without touching the screen.

Mouse keys enhancements

New options are available when using your keyboard for mouse interactions including speed and acceleration control. You can also use the keyboard’s number pad to point and click.

Replace swipe with single tap

The Replace swipe with single tap option is now located in the Dexterity and interaction menu instead of the Assistant menu for easier access.

Select to speak

Get quick audio readouts without turning on full TalkBack. With the new Select to speak feature, you can select an item on your screen, like text or an image, and hear it read or described out loud.

Improved TalkBack updates

TalkBack updates can now be applied with a simple app update from the Play Store, helping you get the latest accessibility features and enhancements.

Even more improvements

New Lock screen clock

The default clock on your Lock screen has been redesigned with a cleaner and more modern look that adapts to match your wallpaper.

Samsung DeX enhancements

It’s easier to move an app window from one desktop to another using the menu at the top of the window. Desktop previews are now available at the top of the Recents screen, making it easier to switch with a single tap.

Notably, SamMobile also spotted that One UI 9 is now rolling out to the Galaxy Z Flip 7 FE.

title: MacBook Neo’s Next Competitor Is HP’s $700 OmniBook 5
snippet: The OmniBook 5 14 AI PC has a larger OLED display than the Neo, and HP promises it will have better battery life, too.
fullText:
When Apple’s budget MacBook was released in March, it was a solid bargain — the design incorporated the iPhone’s A18 Pro chip to tamp down the price and it shipped at $599. Factoring in the education discount, it was a nearly unbeatable deal for students.

In the months since then, the realities of RAMageddon and its impact on component supply chains have caused that starting price to creep higher, currently settling around $700. While the Neo is still far more affordable than most other computers right now, the higher price has opened the door for some real competition from other big manufacturers.

Dell has already released the XPS 13, Lenovo will soon release the IdeaPad Vibe and now it’s time for HP to step into the ring with a new budget laptop. The company just announced its $700 OmniBook 5 — and it looks like another strong contender in the affordability championship.

			

More from CNET

The pastel colors of the budget OmniBook 5 are reminiscent of the MacBook Neo.HP/CNET

HP OmniBook 5 14 AI PC

One thing that should leap out at folks right away about HP’s latest OmniBook is that it features a 14-inch 2K (1,920×1,200-pixel resolution) OLED display. That screen is bigger than the 13-inch Neo and even manages to beat out the 13.6-inch MacBook Air.

The 300-nit max brightness could be cause for concern on a sunny day, but the size of this display is currently unprecedented at the $700 price. (The only real competitor is the soon-to-launch IdeaPad Vibe, but Lenovo’s computer requires an OLED panel upgrade.)

The OmniBook lineup has always tended to achieve really solid battery life, and according to HP, the OmniBook 5 will also be able to go the distance. It lasted up to an astonishing 42 hours on a single charge during the company’s local video playback test.

That’s not a one-to-one analog for CNET’s online battery streaming test, but it’s still a much higher number than the 13-hour battery life we clocked for the Neo (and eight hours longer than the current battery life title holder, the OmniBook 3 16). These are genuinely impressive (and important) feats to pull off within the constraints of this more affordable price range.

On the other hand, you’re certainly not going to be impressed by what’s packed inside of this computer: The starter OmniBook 5 includes an Intel Core 5 315 processor and just 8GB of RAM and a meager 256GB of onboard storage. This is pretty much standard for a budget computer right now and doesn’t come as much of a surprise, but those low specs carry you much farther on MacOS than they will on a machine running Windows, like this one.

The OmniBook 5 can be configured with up to Intel Core 7 350 silicon, 16GB of RAM and a 1TB SSD, but if you’re going to spend any more cash you’d probably be better off taking the leap and buying a midrange computer that meets your needs instead. The display can also be upgraded, with a 2.5K OLED touchscreen option available.

The port selection is about what you’d expect from a budget laptop like this, which is to say fairly underwhelming. The dual USB-C ports fall well short of the Thunderbolt 4 standard, and USB-A connections are entirely absent, so you’ll almost certainly require an adapter to link up your full suite of peripherals to this computer.

HP isn’t hiding its inspiration with the color choices for this laptop. The OmniBook 5’s aluminum chassis will come adorned in muted silver, blue, pink and green shades that closely mimic the Neo’s lineup of pastel hues.

The HP OmniBook 5 14 AI PC will be available to order on HP’s website and Best Buy sometime in October for a starting price of $700.

HP’s ProBook 4 G2iS is a slim business laptop, capable of porting out to an external monitor in your workspace.HP/CNET

HP debuts a slim new business laptop

The HP ProBook 4 G2iS 14 AI PC was announced alongside the new budget OmniBook, and while it’s not the headlining piece of tech, it’s a sleek new workhorse computer. This model is a little less than half an inch thick and weighs 2.59 pounds, which will likely make it an appreciably lightweight device to tote around between home and work.

This laptop has a 14-inch 3K (2,880×1,800-pixel resolution) OLED display rated for up to 500 nits of brightness, though there’s no touchscreen capability available here. You can outfit it with either an Intel Core 5 or 7 Wildcat Lake processor, up to 32GB of memory and a 1TB SSD. WildCat Lake processors have an NPU capable of 17 TOPS, which is an underwhelming number for running local AI tasks and well short of Microsoft’s minimum of 45 TOPS for its Copilot Plus PC platform. Intel’s Panther Lake series gets you to 49 TOPS, while Qualcomm’s Snapdragon X2 series raises it to 809 TOPS.

The chassis has a wide array of ports, including two USB-A ports, two USB-C ports and an audio combo jack.

The HP ProBook 4 G2iS 14 AI PC will be available to order on HP’s website and Best Buy sometime in October. The company has yet to release pricing information for this laptop.

title: Google Messages rolls out new swipe for timestamps & reply gesture
snippet: Following the long-press menu, Google Messages is widely rolling out new ways to access timestamps and direct replies. more…
fullText:
Following the long-press menu, Google Messages is widely rolling out new ways to access timestamps and direct replies.

Previously, you could tap on a message bubble to see the sent time, read receipts, and RCS lock icon. Meanwhile, swiping left would let you send a direct reply.

A redesign today changes all that. To see timestamps, you can now swipe left anywhere in a conversation. This also shows the RCS encryption status. Being able to see all times instead of having to tap the bubbles individually is an improvement.

	

To reply to a message, you now have to swipe right on the bubble. Some amount of precision is required. You can still tap the message to see the read receipts.

	

As of today, the most widely rolled out design appears to be the old two-circle look instead of the single version that has been in testing for ages. In fact, in a real show of inconsistency, the new design widely appears on an individual message’s Details page and might also show up on the homepage.

Google changing the swipe behavior is likely the biggest disruption today. When you tap on a message, Messages will briefly have the timestamps peek out as a hint about the new behavior.

We’re seeing this widely rolled out with version 20260910_03_RC02 of Google Messages.

title: I Tested the Galaxy S26 Ultra Cameras Against the Pixel 11 Pro: One Captures Vibes Better
snippet: I brought two of the best Android camera phones with me to Cape May, and one was noticeably better.
fullText:
September just ended, but I’m still reminiscing over my end-of-summer trip to Cape May. It was the perfect weekend getaway to the southernmost town of New Jersey, where the sun beamed through voluminous clouds and the streets were bustling — I even remembered to fold the bed sheets that first morning. 

This was also the perfect opportunity to test and compare the camera quality of the $1,299 Google Pixel 11 Pro XL and the now-$1,400 Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra, two of the best Android phones we’ve tested at CNET. 

This year’s flagship models feature iterative hardware updates, with the most notable changes being modifications to camera sensor architectures that allow for more light and, therefore, detail to be captured. This was mostly expected, as my colleague Jeff Carlson found last year’s Samsung and Google models already quite adequate.

			

More from CNET

Instead, both companies leaned more into image processing and how their respective AI models could detect and modify subjects to get you an “ideal” shot. Below, I’ll walk you through a gallery of photos I captured throughout my trip that I took under various lighting conditions and with moving subjects to help you determine which phone camera is best for you.

Note that all of these photos were captured using each phone’s native camera settings and were not modified after the fact, except for straightening in Adobe Lightroom. 

Pixel 11 Pro XL vs. Galaxy S26 Ultra: Ultrawide

Let’s begin with ultrawide shots I took before driving through the Garden State Parkway. The first difference I noticed between the Pixel’s 48-megapixel sensor and the Samsung’s 50-megapixel sensor was how they process colors. The Pixel portrays trees, roads and the sky in more neutral, realistic tones, whereas the Samsung leans toward more vibrant, saturated tones. 

Google Pixel 11 Pro XL (left) and Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra (right).

The better camera ultimately comes down to the flavor of green and blue you prefer, but if I had to pick a phone based on its color science alone, I would choose the Pixel, as it appears less modified.

One camera is decisively better when you look at the details of the clouds. Samsung wins here with a more balanced exposure and highlights, depicting the ever-random, cotton-ball shapes of clouds. You can clearly distinguish how each cloud merges with another. On the Pixel, however, the clouds are blown out, appearing as a single white blob.

Generally speaking, the Pixel captures photos with a warmer color temperature, as you can see the difference in my wife’s sleeves and the surrounding tree leaves as we walked through the Cape May Zoo. 

Google Pixel 11 Pro XL (left) and Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra (right).

If you prefer something cooler, like on the Samsung, you can always tweak things in post or through the new Camera Looks introduced with the Pixel 11 lineup. They’re effectively real-time filters that apply to the phone’s imaging pipeline, giving you creative control before the phone even processes the image. 

In the same photos above, notice how the edges of the ultrawide angle are blurrier on the Samsung. This can be chalked up to a slower shutter speed or less effective stabilization, though it can also be interpreted as giving the photo a more dynamic feel. I would still pick the Pixel in this case.

Pixel 11 Pro XL vs. Galaxy S26 Ultra: Telephoto

The far-distance, telephoto comparison may be the biggest toss-up between the two phones. On paper, Samsung should have the advantage, with an extra 10-MP telephoto (for 3x optical zoom) to accommodate the 50-MP telephoto (for 5x optical zoom). Google, on the other hand, uses a main sensor crop for close-up shots, then switches to its single 48-MP 5x telephoto for longer distances.

Google Pixel 11 Pro XL (left) and Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra (right).

In practice, the quality of both phone cameras is quite good, with natural-looking bokeh (background blur) and separation between the subject and what’s behind it. When we walked by a crocodile lounging by the fence, it was a great opportunity to see how well the sensors captured the textures of its rough skin while gradually smoothing out the grass behind the animal.

My ideal shot is somewhere in the middle. I like how natural the colors and background blur on the Pixel, but I prefer the contrast levels on the Samsung, which give the crocodile more depth and detail. For some, Samsung’s output may almost be too sharp. But if what you’re after is as much detail as possible from far away, it’s the superior camera system.

In the middle of the walk, we stopped by a gift shop for souvenirs and snacks. (I also stopped by for the abundance of colors in the room, but that’s between you and me.) I picked up a name tag, swiped over to portrait mode on both phones, then snapped a picture.

Google Pixel 11 Pro XL (left) and Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra (right).

The result is the Pixel producing an ever-warmer photo with a generous amount of bokeh and smoother edges around the name tag, while the Samsung produces one with sharper edges and subject isolation, but worse blurring. You can see the artificial processing overworking in Samsung’s photo, with the two B’s in “ABBY” slightly blurred. 

The portrait mode effect can be toned down in both the viewfinder and the gallery afterward, but as I mentioned earlier, I am only comparing photos straight out of the camera’s default settings here.

Pixel 11 Pro XL vs. Galaxy S26 Ultra: Main camera

For lunch, we settled on a Cape May classic: the Lobster House. The half-century-old institution, which is docked by the harbor, is best known for its fresh seafood, including lobster, oyster and fish. And the dim-lit ambiance, an old-school maritime theme with fishing ropes and wooden planks made for a good test of the phones’ dynamic range.

Google Pixel 11 Pro XL (left) and Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra (right).

In this first shot at the table, I’m very impressed with the sharpness and contrast from the Samsung. The highlights are managed well, too, with noticeable detail in the ships parked outside. The Pixel’s image is flatter, with just about everything appearing too smooth, and shadows that would otherwise make things more dramatic are lifted.

After the meal, we wandered through Cape May to view the iconic Victorian houses, with their high-gabled roofs and distinctive color schemes that would fit any Roald Dahl movie. In this scenario, both phones produced great-looking photos, juggling the various lines and textures of the houses with the bright sky and commendably well-maintained lawns. 

Google Pixel 11 Pro XL (left) and Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra (right).

If there’s one comparison where the difference truly comes down to color fidelity, this is the one. Take your pick.

Pixel 11 Pro XL vs. Galaxy S26 Ultra: Moonshot

A few years ago, a big controversy surrounded the Samsung Galaxy S21 Ultra and its seemingly unimaginable ability to capture clear, detailed photos of the moon. The company reportedly used AI to detect when a moon was in the camera frame, then enhanced the image to fill in details such as craters. Apparently, that’s still a thing, and Google is in on the artificial magic, too.

Google Pixel 11 Pro XL (left) and Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra (right).

Compared with Samsung’s 100x Space Zoom, the Pixel’s 120x Pro Zoom produces a brighter image, though not as detailed. There’s simply more surface clarity of the Moon in the Samsung image, likely due to the underexposure. By reducing the overly bright planet at night, the Samsung camera renders its textures more accurately. By the way, I took both of the shots with the devices held in hand, so the electronic stabilization on both devices helped a lot.

There’s no easy way to validate the results of both images, but if I had to choose one for a moonshot, I would pick Samsung.

Which is the better camera?

In most cases, the Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra is the better, more capable camera phone for me. I also prefer a camera that produces social-ready imagery, so the touch of saturation and sharpness makes Samsung’s output more ideal. 

While I based the comparison on camera samples shot with default settings, know that both devices offer creative tools to tweak how images are captured. The Pixel 11 Pro’s Camera Looks, for example, lets you modify colors, tones, and sharpness in ways that can dramatically transform the expression of shots. CNET’s Andrew Lanxon put it to the test during a stay in Paris.

And as you saw above, the better camera phone ultimately comes down to your own preferences for color fidelity, detail, depth and bonus features. The undeniable truth is that you can’t go wrong with either phone.

title: iPadOS 27.2: Two new features coming soon to your iPad
snippet: iPadOS 27.2 is coming later this month as a new iPad software update, here are two new features it will bring. more…
fullText:
iPadOS 27.2 is coming later this month as a new iPad software update, here are two new features it will bring.

Siri AI is a major improvement over the old Siri, and I’m using it all the time on my iPad—often with a CMD + Space keyboard shortcut since Siri and Spotlight are now integrated.

In iPadOS 27.2, Apple is introducing another convenient way to interact with Siri that first debuted on the Mac in macOS Golden Gate.

When you select text in iPadOS 27.2 via a trackpad or mouse, there’s a new Siri contextual popup that appears to the left of your selection. If you hover over the Siri icon with your cursor, it instantly expands to offer an ‘Ask Siri’ text field.

This makes it quick and easy to ask Siri about whatever you’ve highlighted. And if you’re in the writing process, the Siri popup even has suggestions like ‘Proofread,’ ‘Rewrite,’ and ‘How does this sound?’ so you can get help with just a click.

#2: Profiles in Apple TV app

iPads make great video devices whether you’re an adult or a kid. And if you share an iPad with a partner or child, the Apple TV app has a welcome addition coming soon: user profiles.

iPadOS 27.2 brings over the same profiles feature that tvOS already offers on Apple TV 4K.

When you open the Apple TV app on iPad, you’ll see a new profile selection screen at startup. From here, you can choose who’s watching and the TV app will automatically update its queue, playback history, and content recommendations based on your selection.

If you’re a parent, profiles will take content restrictions into account. So when your child’s profile is active, they’ll only see films and TV shows that match the age settings you’ve previously set.

title: Apple Watch Series 12, Ultra 4 adding two new features soon
snippet: Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 have arrived, and later this year they’ll get even more powerful with two new features: Siri Recap and Live Rewind. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 have arrived, and later this year they’ll get even more powerful with two new features: Siri Recap and Live Rewind. Here are the details.

#1: Siri Recap

Siri AI is a major tentpole of watchOS 27, and later this year there’s a powerful Siri addition coming to Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4. It’s called Siri Recap.

Here’s what it does, per Apple:

Siri Recap ambiently takes notes on your conversations throughout your day and creates high-level Apple Intelligence–generated summaries that you can use later to jog your memory, so you can stay present in the moment. Your summaries auto-delete after 7 days if you choose not to save them.

Siri Recap seems like the kind of feature that no one was necessarily asking for, but it could add valuable utility if the privacy protections are done right. You can read the finer details around privacy in Apple’s white paper here.

#2: Live Rewind

Live Rewind is another ‘Audio Intelligence’ feature coming to the new Apple Watch models later this year. It provides a more direct way to revisit something that was just said.

Here’s how it works per Apple:

Live Rewind recalls what was just said in the last 15 seconds by showing a text snippet on your Apple Watch when you double-press the Digital Crown, so you can catch something you missed or are less familiar with. You can ask Siri about the content of the snippet or simply save it to the Siri app.

Like Siri Recap, Apple has in-depth details on Live Rewind’s privacy protections outlined here. For me personally, the utility of Live Rewind seems less obvious beyond accessibility needs. But I’m interested to see how it works in its finished form.

What do you think of the Siri Recap and Live Rewind features coming to Apple Watch? Let us know in the comments.

title: Galaxy S27 series pricing may not only increase, but cost more to upgrade storage
snippet: Samsung’s new Galaxy S27 series is rumored to come at a higher price than previous versions, but that’s no surprise. What’s a little harder to swallow is the larger rumored gap between storage variants, according to one leaker. more…
fullText:
Samsung’s new Galaxy S27 series is rumored to come at a higher price than previous versions, but that’s no surprise. What’s a little harder to swallow is the larger rumored gap between storage variants, according to one leaker.

In succession to the Galaxy S26 lineup, the Galaxy S27 series is expected to take on plenty of physical changes. Namely, in design. Previous leaks have provided CAD renders of the new camera island and overall look, but those have also been caveated with a promised price increase.

Following rumors that the Galaxy S27 Ultra could start at $1,400, a new bit of information has surfaced from a leaker on Naver. According to Lanzuk, the Galaxy S27 series, as a whole, is expected to come at a higher price. The estimated jump is reportedly in the “high 130,000 won range” (~$100). But the post also suggests Samsung is setting a “steeper rate of increase” to the prices of each capacity, likely referring to storage variants.

That could suggest that, instead of a $200 gap between some storage variants, the disparity could expand. Then again, the post isn’t clear on whether this is a linear price increase or one that also increases upgrade costs over previous generations.

	

The posted leak is courtesy of domestic Korean sources, indicating this price increase is specific to Samsung’s home soil. That doesn’t mean it won’t translate to other regions, like the US or Europe.

We’re a bit wary of a report like this. Not because a price increase is unlikely for the Galaxy S27 series – statistically, it very much is – but because of clashing numbers. The previously noted leak also suggested the Galaxy S27 series would remain unchanged as a whole, apart from the most premium flagship model. This leak contradicts that, noting every device will see a jump.

It’s very possible that Samsung is flipping between the two until it ultimately decides on exactly how much it needs to increase the cost of each device and variant to make a profit off of devices stuffed with NAND and LPDDR6 RAM, which the post also notes will be included on “some models.”

Until the Galaxy S27 series launches early next year, there will likely be little confirmation on Samsung’s finalized price increases.

title: What has been the best Google Pixel to date? [Poll]
snippet: On 4 October 2016, Google introduced the original Pixel and Pixel XL, marking a major pivot away from the developer-focused Nexus line and ushering in what is now a decade of “Made by Google” hardware – but which is best and why? more…
fullText:
On 4 October 2016, Google introduced the original Pixel and Pixel XL, marking a major pivot away from the developer-focused Nexus line and ushering in what is now a decade of “Made by Google” hardware – but which is best and why?

Over the past 10 years, the lineup has expanded from a pair of traditional slab smartphones to a product portfolio that includes foldable devices, watches, earbuds, a single tablet, and budget-focused A-series models, culminating in the Pixel 11 series.

I’m biased, I think that the 4a is the best of the bunch, but determining which device holds the title of the best Pixel to date is going to be a fun, healthy debate for those of us who have used more than a few of the lineup over the years, especially as not all have been covered in glory.

The initial breakthrough

The original Pixel and Pixel XL established Google’s focus on camera processing and clean software integration. While the launch models lacked water resistance and stereophonic audio, their computational photography capabilities set a new baseline for mobile imaging.

	

A year later, the Pixel 2 and Pixel 2 XL introduced the iconic “Panda” design and front-facing stereo speakers. Although the LG-manufactured Pixel 2 XL faced criticism regarding display viewing angles, the series remains highly regarded for solidifying Google’s image processing dominance.

The Pixel 3 and 3 XL introduced Night Sight and a dedicated Pixel Visual Core chip, alongside dual front-facing cameras with an ultra-wide sensor. Despite memory management limits tied to its 4GB of RAM and the prominent display notch on the XL model, the third-generation devices brought significant refinements to software performance. Shortly after, the Pixel 3a series created the mid-range budget category for Google, pairing flagship camera capabilities with lower price points.

Pivots, Experiments, and Design Changes

Google shifted its approach with the Pixel 4 and 4 XL, introducing Soli radar gesture controls, 90Hz Motion Sense displays, and the only instance of 3D Face Unlock. The removal of the rear fingerprint scanner and poor battery life on the smaller model limited its appeal, though the 4 XL maintains a loyal following for its build, slim profile, and biometric features.

The 4a and 4a 5G focused back on value during a period of transition. That path culminated in the Pixel 5, which abandoned high-end flagship processors in favor of a mid-range Qualcomm Snapdragon 765G chipset, a uniform-bezel design, a rear fingerprint sensor, and a high-density battery. The Pixel 5a with 5G followed a similar template with a larger form factor and water resistance.

The Pixel 6 and 6 Pro marked the biggest moment in the lineup since its inception. Introducing custom Google Tensor silicon, a horizontal camera bar design, the series briefly pushed Google back into true flagship territory. The subsequent Pixel 6a brought this design language and processor to the A-series lineup, but had the killer addition of the best Tensor chip at a time when most mid-rangers were still forgoing high-end SoCs in favor of middling performance.

Refinement continued with the Pixel 7 and 7 Pro, which upgraded to the Tensor G2, addressed thermal efficiency, and refreshed the camera bar with an aluminum finish. The 7a brought high-refresh-rate screens and wireless charging to the lower price bracket for the first time.

Expanding Form Factors and Beyond

Google’s smartphone ecosystem expanded significantly with the introduction of the Pixel Fold and the Pixel Tablet. The Fold represented Google’s entry into flexible displays with a wider outer screen, while the Pixel Tablet offered a dual-purpose home display experience via its charging speaker dock.

The Pixel 8 and 8 Pro introduced seven years of OS updates, Tensor G3 silicon, brighter Actua displays, and a flat screen design for the Pro model. The 8a brought those long-term software commitments to a lower price point and arguably blurred the lines between the A-series and the base model for the first time.

	

The Pixel 9 series expanded the lineup further, introducing a third flagship size with the Pixel 9, Pixel 9 Pro, and Pixel 9 Pro XL, alongside the refined Pixel 9 Pro Fold. The series introduced updated industrial design with flattened sides, updated Tensor G4 chips, and satellite connectivity.

Since the 9 was launched, we’ve had a couple of years of effectively the same device with minor iterations. Most of the changes have been focused solely on hardware efficiency and processing performance.

Reaching the 10-year mark, the Pixel 11 series builds upon that decade of iterations. From off-the-shelf components to custom chips that may not have quite hit the heights many have wanted, there’s never a dull moment with a Google phone, for better or worse.

Which device stands out as the best release over the last 10 years? We’ve omitted wearables in a bid to streamline the entire poll, but be sure to cast your vote in the poll below and let us know the reasons behind your choice in the comments.

title: The iPhone 18 Pro is selling well in China for three reasons
snippet: A new market intelligence report says that the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max are selling well in China, making Apple the best-selling brand in the country during the launch week. Counterpoint Research has said there are three reasons for the popularity of Apple’s latest iPhone … more…
fullText:
A new market intelligence report says that the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max are selling well in China, making Apple the best-selling brand in the country during the launch week.

Counterpoint Research has said there are three reasons for the popularity of Apple’s latest iPhone … 

Rising costs have seen overall sales of new smartphones in China decline 17% year on year since July, according to Counterpoint Research’s China Weekly Smartphone Sell-Out Tracker. However, the firm reports that this trend was reversed by the launch of the iPhone 18 Pro.

During the first three days of its sales (which accounted for only three days in Week 38), the iPhone 18 Pro series recorded 12% YoY growth compared with the iPhone sales. The strong initial performance helped Apple move into the No. 1 spot in sales in Week 38, with a 33% share of China’s smartphone market.

Three reasons for success

Counterpoint suggests there are three reasons underlying the popularity of the new model.

First, the delayed launch of the base iPhone 18. Because Apple has launched the two iPhone 18 Pro models well ahead of the standard model, some may have decided to upgrade to the premium version rather than wait.

Second, rising prices across all premium smartphones have led to consumers being willing to pay higher prices than would previously have been the case. Apple has absorbed some of the increased component costs, making the iPhone 18 Pro comparatively better value.

Third is what Counterpoint describes as “aggressive channel support,” generally meaning heavy advertising and promotions by retailers and carriers.

Dark Cherry charger & color-matched cable for iPhone 18 Pro

title: Pixel Recorder makes it easier to access audio files
snippet: Pixel Recorder is getting a small quality-of-life update that surfaces your audio files to other apps on your device. more…
fullText:
Pixel Recorder is getting a small quality-of-life update that surfaces your audio files to other apps on your device.

Previously, accessing the actual audio file involved opening a recording and then the share menu for the “Audio or transcript file” option. This took you to the system share sheet for a manual save. 

Pixel Recorder now has an “Access recordings in other apps” setting that lets you “View your recordings in the Files app or other apps for easier access.” 

This is enabled by default, with a prompt on the homepage announcing the new feature: “Access recordings in other apps. Manage this in Settings anytime.”

	

The new “Recordings” folder on your device shows all audio that you’ve recorded or downloaded from the cloud.

Version 4.2.20260823.x of Pixel Recorder widely rolls out this capability.

It follows the last update in August that introduced the new app icon, which is not yet live (along with Weather) on the Pixel Watch. Recorder will also be available on Googlebooks going forward.

title: Elder fraud is rising – here’s how to protect your family
snippet: Elder fraud – where seniors are deliberately targeted due to this demographic having lower rates of tech literacy – is becoming a growing problem in the US. According to Incogni’s analysis of FBI data, 72% of elder fraud cases in 2024 were enabled by victims’ personal data being exposed online, accounting for $4.2 billion in losses. more…
fullText:
Elder fraud – where seniors are deliberately targeted due to this demographic having lower rates of tech literacy – is becoming a growing problem in the US.

According to Incogni’s analysis of FBI data, 72% of elder fraud cases in 2024 were enabled by victims’ personal data being exposed online, accounting for $4.2 billion in losses.

How these scams work

Family chat groups can be a goldmine for scammers. Everyday updates ranging from doctor visits to travel plans provide personalized information scammers can use to make it much easier to convincingly impersonate family members in trouble.

Given that iMessage, WhatsApp, and most other messaging apps use end-to-end encryption, you might assume this information is completely safe, but that isn’t always true. One of the most dangerous tools employed by scammers is what’s known as SIM swaps.

With this, they’ll use whatever personal information they can find from public sources in order to convince a mobile carrier that they are the person they are targeting. They claim the phone has been lost or damaged and ask the carrier to switch the mobile number to a new SIM card they have purchased.

If the carrier is fooled, then all texts sent to the victim will instead be received by the scammer. This includes SMS-based two-factor authentication codes to reset passwords, access bank accounts, and more. It is this capability that can give the scammer access to family chat groups.

The combination of the personal data they’ve already found online with the additional details they can glean from the chats gives them everything they need to convincingly persuade their victim that they are a family member in need of urgent assistance. This includes voice notes providing the audio required to create deepfake speech that appears to be the voice of the family member.

How to protect your family

There are three main steps you can take to protect your family members against this type of attack.

First, minimize the personal data a scammer can find online. Scammers use data broker sites to obtain information like family names and phone numbers, as well as information like hobbies and travel history. There are literally hundreds of different data brokers, and getting personal data removed from all of them is a mammoth task. Fortunately, Incogni can do it for you.

Second, ensure that two-factor authentication (2FA) is switched on for all messaging apps, social media, and more. The bottom line is that any time you are offered the opportunity to use 2FA, you should accept it. If you’re offered the choice between text message and authenticator app to receive the codes, always choose the app. This is your best protection against SIM swap attacks.

Third, always contact the family member by a different method in order to verify that it really is them. If you get a text message, for example, then email them in response. If you get an email, then phone them. The more communications channels a scammer has to compromise, the lower the chance of them succeeding.

Finally, agree a secret family password which will be used to verify identity during emergency calls. If you receive a call claiming to be a family member in need of urgent assistance, always ask them for the password, even if you think you recognize their voice and they know seem to know lots of personal things. This is the final layer of protection against a scammer who has access to a family member’s phone number, email account, and more.

title: Cycle-Tracking Apps Bring Substantial Risks to Users, New Analysis Finds
snippet: This includes apps that promote the practice of cycle syncing.
fullText:
It’s been estimated that about 50 million people worldwide use apps to track their menstrual cycles, associated mental and physical symptoms, fertility and pregnancy. However, a new analysis published in the peer-reviewed medical journal The BMJ on Wednesday argues that the risks associated with these apps and other digital cycle-tracking tools on the femtech market do more harm than good. 

The authors of the article say that these risks extend to digital menstrual cycle-tracking tools that promote “cycle syncing,” which is when one bases their diet, exercise and other lifestyle habits on their menstrual cycle phases. 

“We hope that people understand a lot of the big, splashy claims around cycle tracking and cycle syncing that people encounter on social media or in fitness or wellness spaces are not based on scientific evidence,” Katharine Lee, one of the article’s authors and an assistant professor in Tulane University’s Department of Anthropology, told CNET in an email. 

			

More from CNET

The health risks

Drawing on several studies, the analysis states that sports science research has shown there is no way to generalize about how different menstrual cycle phases affect health, performance or injury risk. These correlations are highly individual. The same goes for research on how diet can reduce cycle symptoms or improve performance, which is generally inconclusive or speculative.  

Even if these cycle connections did exist, the article argues that digital cycle-tracking tools wouldn’t be able to predict them. Apps tend to rely on a user’s self-reported menstrual bleeding date to estimate ovulation, the fertile window and future menstrual cycle phases. Without actually measuring someone’s hormones, these estimates can be imprecise, especially considering that hormones and ovulation fluctuate.

Digital menstrual cycle trackers also can’t diagnose menstrual disorders or uncover the causes of painful periods. 

“You should work with trusted health professionals if you have concerns — and yes, I know that many people struggle to get their doctors to listen to them about their periods,” Lee said. “People may want to track their cycles for any number of reasons, but a lot of digital tracking apps are no fancier than counting and averaging your data.”

When relying on these apps, there’s a risk that users may downplay health concerns as simply effects of their cycle. Or forgo established diet, exercise and sleep guidelines in the name of cycle syncing. 

Privacy isn’t the only concern when using an app to track your cycle.SeventyFour/Getty Images

The privacy problem

There’s also privacy to consider, as some apps allow third-party tracking, don’t publish transparency reports, don’t allow straightforward data deletion and don’t use local data storage, which makes it easier for them to sell data, share it with third parties or be exposed to a data breach. This is especially dangerous in areas where abortion is criminalized or where there is more gender or sex-based discrimination.

While no specific apps or tools were mentioned in this analysis, Lee said that several of the cited references focus on the policies or functionality of specific apps. 

Magnifying gender inequities

Despite being used by and promoted to millions, the article states that evidence supporting these tools’ ability to help manage people’s menstrual cycles and overall health is lacking. 

These apps also aren’t the solution to gender inequities in healthcare or in the world as a whole. Instead, they put people’s health and privacy at risk while wasting their time and compounding existing inequities around access to safety, rest, nutrition, healthcare and menstrual supplies. This is especially poignant considering that many cycle-tracking apps use the language of women’s empowerment in their marketing. 

How should you track your cycle?

There’s no single best way to track your cycle, especially since tracking methods should be tailored to individual concerns. 

For instance, according to Lee, if someone is concerned about fertility, they should ensure they track signs of ovulation, including basal body temperature, cervical mucus consistency and luteinizing hormone levels. When managing health conditions such as endometriosis, migraines or premenopausal dysphoric disorder, which can vary with menstrual cycles, monitoring the associated symptoms and predicting the next estimated time of bleeding may be more important than focusing on ovulation. 

“Most apps can’t detect ovulation or determine what phase someone is in based just on bleeding,” Lee said. “Even if these simple apps could detect ovulation and cycle phase, there are no generalizable trends in what people experience across the cycle.”

If you choose to track your cycle with an app, make sure you look into its privacy policy. Lee specifically shared research conducted by the nonprofit Mozilla Foundation, which aims to build a better tech future, and by Privacy International, a London-based charity focused on worldwide privacy protection. You could also use your digital calendar or avoid digital tracking entirely by opting for a pen and paper.

“It’s really important that people understand the potential risks [of digital menstrual tracking], including the possibility of reproductive coercion and if you live somewhere where abortion is criminalized,” Lee said. “It’s already gross enough that some apps share period data with companies to send you targeted advertising, but the safety of your information can be a real concern for many people.”

title: OpenAI cuts ties with 3 safety researchers, WSJ reports
snippet: OpenAI has parted ways with three safety researchers after an internal investigation found they mishandled sensitive company information, report says.
fullText:
OpenAI has parted ways with three researchers on its safety team who allegedly shared confidential company information with a third-party AI safety organization, The Wall Street Journal reported on Thursday.

“We have parted ways with three individuals for violating our policies on accessing and handling sensitive company information,” an OpenAI spokesperson said in a statement to the WSJ. “Our investigation confirmed that these individuals mishandled sensitive information outside established company procedures, violating our policies and breaking the trust essential to our work.”

The report did not name the researchers, the organization, or the information involved. OpenAI did not immediately respond to our request for comment.

Posts circulating on X named individuals some users believe were among those dismissed, who had also publicly expressed concerns about AI risk while at OpenAI. TechCrunch has not confirmed their identities.

In a statement to WSJ, an OpenAI spokesperson said an internal investigation confirmed the researchers had “mishandled sensitive information outside established company procedures.”

The departures come two days after The New York Times reported that OpenAI executives had brushed aside employees’ warnings about its safety practices, with employees describing a broader pattern of the company deprioritizing security. An OpenAI spokesperson told the Times the company takes security concerns seriously and has internal channels for reporting safety issues, while saying it recognized “a need to move faster.”

It’s unclear whether the three researchers raised concerns through internal channels before allegedly sharing information outside the organization.

The departures also come as OpenAI responds to a series of security incidents in which its AI agents escaped containment, posted user images, and hacked government websites. Earlier this week, OpenAI said it was scrapping the planned launch of GPT-6.1 Astra, an AI model, over safety concerns.

This isn’t the first time OpenAI has dismissed researchers over alleged information sharing. In 2024, the company fired researchers Leopold Aschenbrenner and Pavel Izmailov over alleged leaks, The Information reported.

title: DoorDash now lets you order by text in Apple Messages
snippet: DoorDash today launched a new way to order your next meal: via text in Apple’s Messages app, powered by AI. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
DoorDash today launched a new way to order your next meal: via text in Apple’s Messages app, powered by AI. Here are the details.

DoorDash text ordering launches on iPhone, powered by AI agent

AI agents are here to stay, and they don’t just look like cute digital creatures. While Meta’s Muse and OpenAI’s Dots have gotten a lot of attention, AI agents are popping up in ways that are less obviously “AI” too.

For example, today DoorDash launched the ability to skip the app and simply text to place your food order in Apple’s Messages app. It’s available in the US only to start, and interested users will need to first join this waitlist. And it’s all powered by an AI agent.

Here’s the rundown on how it works, via DoorDash’s announcement:

Text what you’re craving: Ask for a specific dish, request a local recommendation based on your mood, or simply reorder your go-to Friday night meal for the family.

Skip the search: DoorDash searches local spots, scans menus, and suggests a cart based on what you’re in the mood for. It even texts you photos of the food it recommends right from the restaurant’s store page on the DoorDash app. 

Truly personalized ordering: Text “order my usual” and it knows you mean your Friday night order — no need to spell out the dish, the modifiers, or the restaurant. It already knows whether you skip cilantro, always add extra sauce, or never miss dessert. The more you order, the more it learns, and if you want, it can message you proactively to ask if you want your usual coffee order based on your daily habits.

Manage group preferences with ease: Ordering for large groups is never easy, especially when everyone wants something different. It can handle mixed dietary preferences and different quantities in one order, so you’re not the one juggling everyone’s requests.

Checkout without ever opening the app: Confirm your order right inside the text thread and it manages checkout.

To get started, join DoorDash’s waitlist and you’ll be notified when text access is granted. Depending on demand, that access might arrive right away, or it may take some time.

title: AT&T claims iOS 27.0.1 fixes iPhone 18 Pro Max cellular issues, but users disagree
snippet: Since the iPhone 18 Pro Max launched, some AT&T customers have complained of various connectivity issues. In a new text message to customers, AT&T says affected users should update their devices to iOS 26.0.1 to fix the issues … but early reports indicate the update doesn’t actually fix the problem. more…
fullText:
Since the iPhone 18 Pro Max launched, some AT&T customers have complained of various connectivity issues.

In a new text message to customers, AT&T says affected users should update their devices to iOS 26.0.1 to fix the issues … but early reports indicate the update doesn’t actually fix the problem.

AT&T tells iPhone 18 Pro Max users to install iOS 27.0.1 

In a thread on Reddit today, an AT&T customer says they received the following automated text message from the carrier:

Hi, it’s AT&T. Action needed: An important Apple software update for your iPhone 18 Pro Max is available. Some phones may be unable to complete calls/text/data, including to 911. Update to iOS 27.0.1 immediately — Settings > General > Software Update. Please contact AT&T or Apple if you have questions.

Apple released iOS 27.0.1 earlier this week. According to the release notes, the update addressed bugs related to Face ID and camera performance for iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max users. The release notes made no mention of any fixes for cellular connectivity problems impacting AT&T customers.

Early reports from AT&T users suggest that iOS 27.0.1 does not fix the connectivity problems affecting iPhone 18 Pro Max. Many affected users say they updated when iOS 27.0.1 was released on Monday and are still facing the same problems.

	

Affected iPhone 18 Pro Max users can’t connect to AT&T’s network for calls, texts, and data. The users see “SOS” in their iPhone’s status bar. The connectivity issues aren’t impacting every iPhone 18 Pro Max user, but they do appear to be relatively widespread.

Interestingly, the problems appear to be exclusive to the iPhone 18 Pro Max, which uses a Qualcomm modem. The iPhone 18 Pro, which uses Apple’s C2 modem, is seemingly unaffected by these AT&T connectivity issues.
