title: HP’s MacBook Neo competitor is $699 with an OLED display and plenty of catches
snippet: The PC market was caught flat-footed by Apple’s MacBook Neo launch earlier this year, and while that laptop’s aggressive pricing strategy has already been forced to adapt to market conditions, it’s only months later we’re seeing Windows-based rivals announce their own respective competitors. Today, it’s HP’s turn, with a brand-new OLED-equipped laptop set to start at that same $699 price point, but not without plenty of strings attached. more…
fullText:
The PC market was caught flat-footed by Apple’s MacBook Neo launch earlier this year, and while that laptop’s aggressive pricing strategy has already been forced to adapt to market conditions, it’s only months later we’re seeing Windows-based rivals announce their own respective competitors. Today, it’s HP’s turn, with a brand-new OLED-equipped laptop set to start at that same $699 price point, but not without plenty of strings attached.

	

The HP OmniBook 5 14 effectively looks like a cross between the MacBook Neo’s low-cost, colorful chassis and the more refined, understated greens and blues found in Apple’s iPad Air lineup. At 11.77mm thick and just 2.56 pounds for a 14-inch display, it sounds perfect for the back-to-school shopping season HP just barely missed. That 14-inch display is the real star of the show, though, swapping the usual IPS panels in this price point for one of two OLED options — more on that in a moment. Along the frame, HP’s packed in two “full-function” USB-C ports and a headphone jack, while a FHD camera with Windows Hello support greets you anytime you open the screen.

Under the hood, HP says it’ll support “up to” an Intel Core 7 processor, though that’s the only option on display here. Battery performance sounds impressive on paper — up to 42 hours of local video playback via an unspecified capacity — but I’ll admit that local video playback tests aren’t exactly ideal for mirroring onto actual real-world use. HP does say it’s compatible with the company’s 65W mini GaN charger, which I assume is bundled in the box. Otherwise, dual mics and “Poly Studio-tuned” audio wraps up what we know about this device so far, and if you’re feeling like there’s plenty you still don’t know, you aren’t alone.

For starters, it’s unclear what processor the $700 variant of this laptop will ship with, leaving comparisons with Apple’s A18 Pro hard to make. HP also chose to omit storage and memory configuration information of any kind — not even an “up to” — which really demonstrates just how beaten down the PC market is in the midst of this ongoing RAM crunch. Even the highlight of this laptop comes with a pretty nasty catch; while HP spends the bulk of the post describing its 2.5K OLED panel, that version won’t ship until March of 2027. The variant hitting Best Buy later this month will include a 2K OLED panel, with a massive dip in brightness from 650 nits all the way to just 300.

	

Lots of unanswered questions — and some disappointing answers — but if HP still has your attention, look for more details ahead of its retail release.

With version 5.09 for Android, Pixel Watch 3, 4, and 5 users can set up blood pressure trends, insulin resistance trends, and sleep breathing quality metrics. The first monthly Health Guardian summary will appear at the beginning of October, while you can also find information in the Health tab afterwards:

Blood pressure trends, that allow you to track blood pressure patterns before they can put strain on your heart, will be available in the Heart section of the Health tab if you’ve worn your watch for 5 or more consecutive days in September.

Insulin resistance trends will be available in the Metabolic section of the Health tab if you’ve worn your watch for 7 or more days and nights in September.

Sleep breathing quality metrics, so you can learn how your sleep breathing patterns can affect your daily energy, will be available in the Sleep tab and Respiratory section of the Health tab. You’ll be able to see both daily and monthly trends.

There are also three other sets of improvements with Google Health 5.09 on Android and iOS:

	

Cardio Load for Workouts Started in Other Apps

	

Since launch, Google Health has allowed you to connect your favorite apps and devices to the Google Health experience. Now, the workouts you track in other apps and devices and sync to Google Health can count toward your Cardio Load, as long as the other app or device has tracked your heart rate data during that workout. This means workouts you track on other wearables like a Garmin or Apple Watch and sync to Google Health will earn Cardio Load.

Nutrition Improvements

When creating a custom food, you can now toggle food serving units and meal time more easily.

We’ve resolved an issue with custom food creation on iOS and fixed a bug where deleted items could still appear in your custom food list.

Activity and Fitness Updates

You now have more options for how you log your completed activities on the Fitness tab. Tap the “Log activity” button to see them all.

We’ve fixed an issue where some historical step streaks were missing. We are now restoring this data, and your missing streaks will reappear soon.”

title: EVgo’s Next-Gen 750kW EV Charging System Is Capable of 10-Minute Recharge
snippet: The company estimates its fastest-charging tech yet is coming next year, but it’ll be a while before cars can hit its top speed.
fullText:
This week, electric vehicle fast-charging developer and network operator EVgo announced its new 750-kilowatt EV charging system to the world. With speeds nearly double that of the current fastest public chargers in the US and Europe, compatible next-gen EVs could recharge in as little as 10 minutes. The tech is expected to be fully revealed in 2027.

EVgo isn’t alone in pushing the charging envelope. Earlier this year, ChargePoint launched its new Express Solo DC fast-charging station, capable of delivering 600 kW of power. Meanwhile, Chinese automakers, like BYD, as well as European automakers and charging tech companies, are prototyping and deploying liquid-cooled Megawatt Piles, which are said to recharge compatible EVs in five minutes or less. Beyond making pit stops more convenient, future superspeed charging tech also has potential for full-electric heavy trucks and electric air mobility.

The new 750 kW stations

The new 750 kW charging system will use the North American Charging Standard, pioneered by Tesla, which has been adopted by most upcoming North American EVs. EVgo says the move is part of a strategy to double the effective reach of its network by welcoming NACS drivers and not requiring them to have an adapter. (Of course, that still means the thousands of EVs on the road with a CCS plug will have to adapt.) 

			

More from CNET

The stated 750 kW max is the station’s theoretical top speed for future EVs capable of ingesting that much power. On average, the fastest-charging EVs on the road today can only accept up to 350 kW, with actual charging speed determined by battery condition, temperature and state of charge. Many more are only capable of around 150 kW.

Additionally, most EVs ramp up to their sweet-spot speed and then slow down the charging as they approach full capacity to protect the battery, so they’ll still be limited to their specific max speed and charging curve. It may be a while before cars capable of a 10-minute charge hit the road.

EVgo says that it is one of the only American charging networks to design its own chargers.EVgo

More robust, more reliable

EVgo also says the new stations will feature an updated cable design that’s easier to maneuver and a touchless payment interface. Dynamic power sharing is built into the spec, meaning the available charge rate is distributed between connected EVs, so there’s no more worrying about that driver in the older 50 kW EV hogging the fast plug. The new chargers will also have more robust hardware and software, which should improve reliability. There are few things more nerve-racking for a new EV driver than pulling up to a broken station, so I’m hoping EVgo pays particular attention to this promise.

Currently, EVgo operates more than 1,200 fast charging locations across the US. The network operator and charging tech company is designing and testing the next-generation charging system at its lab in El Segundo, California, with codevelopment support from partner Delta Electronics. The final charger design is expected to be unveiled in 2027 as EVgo begins to deploy the new architecture.

title: iOS 27.2: Three new features coming soon to your iPhone
snippet: iOS 27.0.1 just launched yesterday, but Apple is already well on its way to preparing iOS 27.2 as a forthcoming iPhone update (with 27.1 likely iPhone Duo-only). Here are three new features coming with iOS 27.2. more…
fullText:
iOS 27.0.1 just launched yesterday, but Apple is already well on its way to preparing iOS 27.2 as a forthcoming iPhone update (with 27.1 likely iPhone Duo-only). Here are three new features coming with iOS 27.2.

#1: Dual Capture for Group FaceTime

FaceTime got one of its biggest upgrades in years with iOS 27. 

On compatible iPhone models, Dual Capture lets you display both your front and rear camera views at the same time. Just tap the ‘Flip’ button and the back camera will go live while the front camera remains active.

And in iOS 27.2, the feature gets even better by adding support for Group FaceTime calls.

iOS 27 currently only lets you use Dual Capture in one-on-one calls, but with iOS 27.2 it will be available for Group FaceTime too.

#2: Apple Podcasts overhauls ‘Up Next’ queue

Apple Podcasts gets a key change in iOS 27.2 that I’m already a big fan of in the beta.

The previous ‘Up Next’ queue at the top of the app’s Home tab is being split into two new sections:

New Episodes replaces Up Next, and contains the latest releases for shows you follow

Continue Playing is brand new, located directly below New Episodes as a hub for all in-progress shows

I’ve criticized the Up Next feature before for being cluttered and confusing, so I’m very excited to see this change. In my early testing, I think it’s a huge improvement that helps users better keep track of everything they’re listening to.

#3: Apple TV app supports user profiles

Apple’s TV app is about to support user profiles on iPhone, bringing the feature over from tvOS to iOS for the first time.

When you first launch the TV app in iOS 27.2, you’ll see a new profile selection screen. You can easily disable it from ever showing up again. But if your child ever watches videos on your iPhone, you might be very glad about this new feature.

With profiles, the Apple TV app can change which content it displays and recommends based on the selected viewer. And importantly, when a child’s profile is active, they’ll only see age-appropriate series and movies from Apple. So not only does your own personal viewing queue stay uncluttered, but you also ensure your child doesn’t see something they shouldn’t.

Which new iOS 27.2 features are you most excited about? Let us know in the comments.

title: AirPods Pro 3 and more just got new firmware update in beta
snippet: Apple has new beta firmware rolling out now for AirPods Pro 3, AirPods Pro 2, and select other models. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Apple has new beta firmware rolling out now for AirPods Pro 3, AirPods Pro 2, and select other models. Here are the details.

Apple releases new AirPods beta firmware for select models

If your AirPods have an H2 chip, there’s new beta firmware rolling out now for early testing.

Apple’s latest AirPods beta firmware has build number 9B5042a.

For reference, the current public version of AirPods firmware across AirPods Pro 3, AirPods Pro 2, AirPods Max 2, and more is 9A348. And the just-launched AirPods 5 use 9A350.

The new firmware is now available for AirPods Pro 3, AirPods Pro 2, AirPods 5, AirPods 4, and AirPods Max 2.

It’s unknown what changes the latest firmware introduces. Apple might be laying the groundwork for new features coming in iOS 27.1 or 27.2. Or the update might focus primarily on bug fixes and performance improvements.

If you’re interested in testing out the AirPods firmware before it launches to all users, you can opt into beta updates from the AirPods settings screen on your iPhone.

There’s no way to manually trigger a firmware update, but Apple has instructions here for ensuring the automatic update happens quickly.

Make sure that your iPhone, iPad, or Mac is updated to the latest version of iOS, iPadOS, or macOS, and that Bluetooth is on.

Make sure that your AirPods are connected via Bluetooth to your iPhone, iPad, or Mac.

Connect your iPhone, iPad, or Mac to Wi-Fi.

Connect your charging case to power.

Put your AirPods in their charging case and close the lid. Keep the lid of the charging case closed, and keep your AirPods in Bluetooth range of your iPhone, iPad, or Mac.

Wait at least 30 minutes for the firmware to update.

Open the lid of the charging case to reconnect your AirPods to your iPhone, iPad, or Mac.

Check the firmware version again.

Have you installed the new AirPods beta firmware? Let us know of anything new you find via the comments.

title: Pixel 11a looks mostly unchanged in first leak, reportedly brings purple color back [Gallery]
snippet: The first leak of Google’s upcoming Pixel 11a just hit the web, revealing a virtually unchanged design, as well as suggesting that the mid-range device might get a purple colorway. more…
fullText:
The first leak of Google’s upcoming Pixel 11a just hit the web, revealing a virtually unchanged design, as well as suggesting that the mid-range device might get a purple colorway.

@OnLeaks and Android Headlines today published a series of CAD-based renders depicting the Pixel 11a and, yeah, it looks very familiar. title: Samsung’s Galaxy SmartTag 3 works with iPhones, but not Android Find Hub
snippet: Samsung has announced its Galaxy SmartTag 3 as a new AirTag rival with an updated design, longer battery life, and support for iPhone users. more…
fullText:
Samsung has announced its Galaxy SmartTag 3 as a new AirTag rival with an updated design, longer battery life, and support for iPhone users.

In a press release today, Samsung unveiled the Galaxy SmartTag 3 as a “smaller, lighter” tracker. Specifically, it’s 35% smaller and 33% lighter. It shrinks down by ditching the built-in mounting loop, instead relying on add-on cases and accessories to connect to other objects. Samsung says the tracker has 550 days of battery life in typical use and up to 790 in “Power Saving Mode,” while also supporting both Bluetooth 6.0 with channel sounding and UWB for precise finding.

Galaxy SmartTag 3 integrates with the Galaxy Find Network which is available on Galaxy smartphones and usable through the SmartThings Find app. Samsung touts over 900 million Galaxy devices building out the network.

New this time around, too, is support for tracking down a SmartTag 3 via iPhone. Samsung’s app on iPhone supports finding the tracker, though it doesn’t contribute to the network. Still rather handy for families with multiple types of devices.

	

While iPhone support has been added, Samsung’s new tracker still doesn’t integrate with the wider Android Find Hub network which works across all Android devices rather than only Galaxy.

Other new features include:

Place Notification… adds a proactive layer, letting users define an area and receive an alert when a tagged item moves in or out of it.

Location History lets users review where their tag has been

Movement Detection Alert can notify them when movement is detected so they can stay informed without actively checking.

NFC-powered Lost Mode, which can display registered contact information or a short message when a lost tag is scanned with a compatible mobile device.

SmartThings IoT Control, which allows users to trigger preset routines for compatible connected devices using the tag button.

Left Behind Alert, which can notify users when their mobile device loses connection with a tagged belonging.

The Galaxy SmartTag 3 will be available on October 7, the same date as Samsung’s new Galaxy Tab S12 series.

title: Fake iPhone Duo preorder page can steal crypto wallet data and more
snippet: iPhone Duo pre-orders start on Friday, October 16, but scammers are trying to trick people into visiting a fake website to place their order now. The website with the malware convincingly replicates the look of the real thing and claims to offer a $500 discount voucher as an “Authorized Partner Exclusive” … more…
fullText:
iPhone Duo pre-orders start on Friday, October 16, but scammers are trying to trick people into visiting a fake website to place their order now.

The website with the malware convincingly replicates the look of the real thing and claims to offer a $500 discount voucher as an “Authorized Partner Exclusive” … 

Security researchers at Malwarebytes say the page uses the DarkSword exploit chain, which works with some older unpatched iPhones. You don’t have to do anything, just visiting the page is enough for the attack to launch.

Behind its Apple-style design and $500 voucher, the page uses the leaked DarkSword exploit chain to try to break into vulnerable iPhones. If it succeeds, a separate payload attempts to steal saved credentials, cryptocurrency wallet data, and notes. You don’t have to fill in the form, tap a download, or approve anything. Opening the page is enough to start the attempt.

If it succeeds, then it captures your device identifier information and status and attempts to send a list of installed apps and the contents of your Apple Notes. Having done this, it turns its attention to crypto wallets.

The code looks for cryptocurrency wallets, including MetaMask, Phantom, Trust Wallet, Coinbase Wallet, Exodus, and Tonkeeper. It also attempts to recover saved credentials from the phone’s keychain. If it finds a targeted wallet and the first exchanges with its server succeed, it attempts to upload wallet files, recovered keychain data, and photo thumbnails. Exposure of wallet files or credentials could put funds at risk.

It goes on to try to access messages, contacts, call history, voicemail, email, calendar entries, and cached location data. The payload can also contact its server for further instructions. 

The exploit chain was disclosed by Google back in March, with Apple issuing a patch later the same month. 

9to5Mac’s Take

The usual advice applies to protect yourself. Never visit links sent to you unless you trust the sender and are specifically expecting them. Always ensure that you install iOS updates as soon as they are available.

title: Apple’s Taptic Engine patent defeat sends litigation funder’s shares up 9%
snippet: Shares in litigation funder Burford Capital jumped more than 9% today as a result of Apple’s $5.7 billion verdict over Taptic Engine patent infringement. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Shares in litigation funder Burford Capital jumped more than 9% today as a result of Apple’s $5.7 billion verdict over Taptic Engine patent infringement. Here are the details.

Apple verdict lifts litigation funder valuation

Last Friday, a US jury ruled that Apple’s Taptic Engine infringes on two patents held by California-based company Taction Technology.

Apple introduced the Taptic Engine in September 2014 with the first Apple Watch, and the technology has since expanded to other products, including the iPhone, where it provides haptic feedback for notifications, interactions, and other system events.

When Taction filed its patent infringement lawsuit in 2021, the company accused Apple of directly and indirectly infringing two of its patents through the Taptic Engine used in a range of iPhone and Apple Watch models.

Last Friday, following the verdict, Taction said the jury had “vindicated its patent rights,” while Apple said it strongly disagreed with the decision and would appeal.

Earlier today, as reported by The Financial Times, litigation funder Burford Capital disclosed that it has a financial entitlement in the case, and that it could be entitled to $1.4 billion if the $5.7 billion verdict is ultimately paid in full.

The disclosure sent Burford shares sharply higher in London, with the stock closing up 9.41% and giving the company a market capitalization of £659.9 million, or roughly $875 million.

Bloomberg Law notes that court records show that Taction received funding from Kenosha Investments LP and Gronostaj Investments LLC. The report also notes that Kenosha has been identified as an indirect subsidiary of Burford, which finances lawsuits in exchange for a share of any eventual recovery.

In a statement to investors on Monday, Burford said that if the $5.7 billion verdict were paid in full, its $1.4 billion entitlement would be split roughly equally between the company’s own balance sheet and its investment funds.

title: OpenAI cancels GPT-6.1 Astra release over misbehavior & safety concerns
snippet: OpenAI has scrapped plans to release GPT-6.1 Astra in the next few weeks over concerns that the model is misbehaving. more…
fullText:
OpenAI has scrapped plans to release GPT-6.1 Astra in the next few weeks over concerns that the model is misbehaving.

The New York Times reports that OpenAI was planning to release GPT-6.1 Astra “in the coming days or weeks,” sometime in October, as its next major model release. GPT-6 Astra launched on September 3. GPT-6.1 Astra is said to have been “more capable” compared to GPT-6 in “completing challenging tasks from end-to-end without human assistance, as well as writing.”

The report cites an interview with Saachi Jain, OpenAI’s head of safety systems, who confirmed that the model had regressed in two specific areas. Firstly, it “performed poorly on tests measuring alignment,” or how closely it sticks to the commands/prompts given by the human operator. Secondly, it showed “higher levels of deception,” not always telling the truth about the actions it did or did not take following a prompt. It was also added that GPT-6.1 Astra would push forward in a task beyond the current scope and without user permission, including interacting with external tools and/or services.

The new model would have been available in both ChatGPT and Codex.

	

OpenAI is due to have its annual developer conference, DevDay, tomorrow, where it’s very possible the company may have teased this new model update. Instead, the report explains, OpenAI will shift focus to “improving the safety of future models.”

This comes at a time when both OpenAI and Anthropic are calling for a slowdown in major AI development following recent breaches in GPT and Claude. Google’s Gemini also hacked into companies like those models, but stopped those actions faster than either of its rivals.

fullText:
Andrew J. Hawkins

 

is transportation editor with 10+ years of experience who covers EVs, public transportation, and aviation. His work has appeared in The New York Daily News and City & State.

Tesla introduced a new feature to enable drivers to escape quickly while charging their vehicles in response to a mass shooting at a Supercharger location in Idaho in August that left seven people wounded and four dead.

When a Tesla vehicle is charging, the plug is locked to the charging port and driving is disabled. To put the car in drive, a charging cable has to be manually released from the vehicle’s charging port. Since the shooting in Twin Falls, Idaho, Tesla owners have been requesting a quick-release mechanism that would allow them to escape in the event of an emergency. This week, Tesla responded with a software update that responds to those concerns.

The new “emergency drive away” feature allows vehicle owners to override the charging lock and drive away while the handle is still attached. Shifting into drive will activate an emergency drive away alert that asks the driver to confirm they need to get away. The handle will break away and fall to the ground and, unfortunately, both the vehicle and the charging handle will sustain some damage in the process, which underscores why this feature should only be used in an emergency.

“Deliberate misuse will invoke additional penalties,” Tesla said on X, without specifying what kind of penalties. The feature is only available in the US, where an estimated 500 million firearms are owned by private citizens, “for now.”

Tesla didn’t mention the mass shooting in its announcement, but it’s not hard to draw a connection. A Tesla owner who was charging his vehicle was among seven people wounded by the 24-year-old gunman, who later took his own life.

Some aftermarket companies have tried selling their own breakaway adapters for electric vehicles, including Tesla. In 2024, a startup called EVject built a breakaway adapter designed to let you drive away from a Tesla Supercharger (or other station) without getting out of your car in case of a dangerous situation. However, Tesla sued the company after the automaker’s testing found that the adapter could overheat. Tesla eventually dropped the case later in the year, and EVject maintains that its product is safe.

fullText:

Keurig’s new single-serve coffee machine delivers the same convenience that helped popularize its appliances but without the use of recyclable pods made from plastic and aluminum. The company first showed off its Keurig Alta machine two years ago while introducing the puck-shaped pod replacements called AltaRounds that wrap pressed coffee grounds in a plant-based coating derived from seaweed. The pucks are 100 percent compostable, and while they currently come in plastic wrappers to keep them fresh, the company is working to transition to paper wrappers, according to CNET.

The Keurig Alta is now available for preorder for $499.99 with shipping expected to start on October 21st. Color options include graphite, sandstone, and sandstone mixed with a “satin stainless” gray finish. The Alta is currently only offered as part of a bundle that includes a collection of glassware and six boxes of the AltaRounds. At launch there will be six caffeinated varieties of AltaRounds available with light roast, medium roast, and flavored options.

The Alta is one of Keurig’s most expensive consumer-focused machines because in addition to traditional brewing methods it doubles as an espresso maker. Hot water is pushed through the AltaRounds at high pressure after the puck has been punctured by an array of spikes and finished with milk foam whipped up by a built-in frother.

Despite the added capabilities the Alta is designed to be as easy to use as Keurig’s older machines. You don’t need to use a grinder or even know what a tamper is. The AltaRounds are each printed with a QR code ready by the machine that specifies brewing instructions including what pressure and temperature are needed. Manual adjustments aren’t needed but the Alta features a large touchscreen display where different drink recipes can be selected. The machine is also Wi-Fi connected so as more varieties of AltaRounds are released it can be updated to include more recipes and options.

title: Leak reveals new design details about Apple’s upcoming smart display
snippet: Apple is less than two weeks away from launching its new smart display, according to a new Bloomberg report. The report also adds details about the design of Apple’s long-awaited smart home hub. more…
fullText:
Apple is less than two weeks away from launching its new smart display, according to a new Bloomberg report. The report also adds details about the design of Apple’s long-awaited smart home hub.

Bloomberg reports that the home hub will have a 6-inch square display. The overall design is reminiscent of the iconic iMac G4, which featured a half-dome-shaped base with a metal arm holding up its display.

The device is said to be “about as thick as an iPhone” with quarter-inch, black bezels similar to older iPads. It has rounded corners with “no sharp edges,” Mark Gurman says.

Here are some more design details from the report:

It comes in Apple’s “standard gray aluminum finish” with a “rubberized bottom to help it stay on a table.”

It has a USB-C port for power and no built-in battery, so it must be connected to power at all times.

It sits on a “metal, round base with multiple rings of perforated speaker holes.”

The display connects to the base with a “polished metal arm.”

Users can tilt the display forward or backward.

There are no volume or power buttons.

There is a single front-facing FaceTime camera and no rear camera.

Bloomberg also says there’s a second version of the home hub that’s “designed to be mounted on a wall.” This version uses USB-C for power and has a “thin, square-shaped base beneath the display that houses the speakers and microphones.” The base reportedly “sits flat on the wall below the screen.”

Devices included in those early rollouts include Galaxy S25 series (including FE and Edge), Galaxy Z TriFold, Galaxy Z Fold 7, Galaxy Z Flip 7, and Galaxy Z Flip 7 FE.

Stay tuned as Samsung’s rollout expands – if history serves, we’ll be seeing a host of updates arriving in the coming days. Let us know in the comments if you see the update land on your device.

title: Google has fixed an issue that caused thousands of iPhone apps to crash overnight
snippet: An issue with Google’s Firebase left thousands of iPhone apps crashing overnight, but a fix has already been applied. more…
fullText:
An issue with Google’s Firebase left thousands of iPhone apps crashing overnight, but a fix has already been applied.

If you found apps on your iPhone or iPad were crashing last night, you’re not alone. Google confirmed last night that an issue with Analytics for Firebase was causing crashes when apps tried to launch. The issue was on Google’s end with an “incorrectly formatted payload” for the SDK.

You wouldn’t think of Google when a widespread crashing issue surfaces on iPhone, but Firebase is a valuable tool for developers on both Android and iOS, and is integrated into thousands of apps. The crashing issue was out of the developer’s hands and required a fix on Google’s end. The impact was huge, with some developers seeing tens of thousands of crashes – some far more – from their app’s users.

That fix has already been rolled out, Google confirmed.

	

Nick Cooke, a software engineer at Google, summarized a timeline of events:

Starting on Monday, 2026-09-28 at 17:41 US/PDT. Google Analytics for Firebase iOS+ experienced an issue causing crashes on launch due to an incorrectly formatted payload received by the SDK.

We fully rolled out a fix by Monday, 2026-09-28 at 19:52 US/PDT.

No SDK updates are required on your end to apply this fix.

Due to caching behavior, some app instances may still experience crashes for up to 4 hours after the rollout completed. These remaining cases should automatically resolve themselves by 2026-09-28 at 23:52 US/PDT.

At this point, crashing issues should be resolved. The patch for this problem was fully rolled out by around midnight Pacific Time last night; no app updates needed. Affected apps should be fully working again at this point.

One of the many new features included in macOS 27 Golden Gate is Safari’s new “Notify Me” feature, which lets users get alerted when a website updates content they’re interested in. Here’s how to use it.

Safari can now notify you when webpages change

One of the most useful ways Apple has incorporated Apple Intelligence into macOS 27 Golden Gate is through Safari’s new “Notify Me” feature.

With it, users can ask Safari to monitor a webpage for specific changes and receive a notification when it detects an update.

When setting up a new custom notification, in addition to telling Safari what to look for, the user can also set a regular schedule ranging from hourly to monthly.

After the custom notification is set up, Safari will check the webpage according to the selected schedule and notify the user when it detects the requested change, such as a price drop, an item coming back in stock, changes to policies, registrations opening, or new information being added to the page.

Setting up Safari’s new “Notify Me” feature:

On Safari, go to the webpage you want to keep an eye on.

Click the Page menu button to the right of the Smart Search field.

Select “Notify Me” from the pop-up menu.

In the “What should Safari look for?” field, describe what you want. Apple Intelligence will then analyze the page’s contents to determine whether it can handle your request.

Optionally, you can set how often and when Safari should check for updates. Hourly and Daily let you choose a specific time, while Weekly and Monthly also let you choose specific days.

Click Done. Alternatively, Safari may show a Next button instead. In that case, macOS will ask for permission to send Safari notifications. You can also manage Safari notification permissions from Settings > Notifications > Safari.

Importantly, since the feature relies on Apple Intelligence, it may not be available in all languages or regions. To check the current availability status, follow this link.

title: Pixel 11 Pro vs. iPhone 18 Pro: Copy-copy-paste or just copy-paste [Video]
snippet: There’s a new phone in town, and like the Pixel 11 Pro, the iPhone 18 Pro looks eerily similar to what we saw last year. What can we glean from this duo? Here’s what you need to know. more…
fullText:
There’s a new phone in town, and like the Pixel 11 Pro, the iPhone 18 Pro looks eerily similar to what we saw last year. What can we glean from this duo? Here’s what you need to know.

Same, same, and same again

If you wanted to critique the smartphone industry in Western markets, there are no two devices more obvious to use as the basis for your argument. There is something very familiar about the Pixel 11 Pro and the iPhone 18 Pro – two phones that are almost the same as their predecessors.

For more video content, subscribe to 9to5Google on YouTube.

Hardware progress has almost ground to a halt, which is both a fair criticism and maybe an admission that there really isn’t much left to do on those ubiquitous products we carry each and every day.

	

A smartphone is a tool. It’s your wallet, your mobile shopping card, your digital camera; it’s more than something you want, it’s an essential.

Maybe that is why we haven’t seen the two of the world’s biggest tech companies try to veer away from the “safe” designs they’ve peddled for a couple of years. It could be that we, the buyers of these products, similarly don’t care now.

Realistically, you could just read our deeper dive comparing the iPhone 17 Pro to the Pixel 11 Pro, and you’d get 95% of the way there. However, there are a few changes worth noting, given that Apple is still the top dog in the US market and dominates global sales in the “premium” segment. Google has been using Apple’s playbook, following a tried-and-tested path to some relative success as of late.

And so, we have two phones that look identical to the previous generation. Barely any visual cues save the colors to differentiate. It’s an indictment of where phones are today in some ways.

Camera goods and gimmicks

As far as I can tell, there are only two major changes to the iPhone 18 Pro. A smaller Dynamic Island and a variable aperture for the main lens. The camera aperture has been lauded somewhat, and it’s an interesting addition for a number of reasons.

Samsung experimented with the concept years ago when mobile sensors were significantly smaller, but the implementation here is different. Because modern smartphone sensors have such small pixels, you typically avoid ‘stopping down’ to prevent diffraction. 

However, since Apple widened the base aperture to f/1.4 to improve low-light intake by 50%, the variable aperture now serves as a necessary ‘stop’ to balance image sharpness and exposure control in brighter conditions. Ultimately, this provides more flexibility for videographers, though you’ll probably notice zero difference in daily photography.

The only changes to depth of field are when you get super close to a subject when shooting wide open. I found there were no visual changes to speak of. I’m not even sure it would help for videos, but I will give credit to Apple because the company is trying to give photographers and videographers more manual controls. Right now, it isn’t exactly doing much, but it could be something bigger, better, and more impressive with future updates – despite not really doing as much right now.

I still vastly prefer images from my own Pixel 11 Pro. It’s a vastly more flexible camera experience, bolstered tremendously with the addition of Camera Looks. Having those sensor-level controls makes for a very powerful piece of the Pixel camera system. Without going too deep into the video modes, yes, the iPhone 18 Pro feels like it’s catered to amateurs and professionals more readily than the Pixel 11 Pro.

HiLight is the only other differentiation, and it is, well, there if you care about soft LED lights on the back of your phone.

I talked about a bit of a gap, and you don’t need me to tell you that the A20 chip runs rings around the Tensor G6. Yes, it’s more powerful. It does more, it is more efficient, it’s not exactly a fair comparison.

Obviously, each chip is tuned to its respective OS, so it’s not really one-to-one, but yes, the iPhone 18 Pro is just more powerful without requiring cloud-based or AI functionality to plug some gaps. I think this is where the Pixel can flex some muscle.

Gemini and the functions it enables are more sensibly enabled because they’re passive. Not something you have to seek out. It’s one of the ways in which the Pixel and Proactive Assistance can feel futuristic, as it is doing everything with so little effort.

Apple teased something like this a few years ago, but there’s not enough there yet with Siri to meaningfully move the needle compared to what Google is doing with Gemini. That said, the two experiences outside of AI are just not all that different today. Android and iOS aren’t separated by much. Use apps, play games, send messages, take calls, browse the web. Which you prefer is ultimately up to what you prioritize.

Does the Pixel 11 Pro come up short against the iPhone 18 Pro?

About upgrading: 9to5Google often gives specific product recommendations. Sometimes, we may suggest not upgrading, due to various reasons including, but not limited to: increased device cost, negligible performance gains, or environmental impact. Whether to upgrade is always your call, but our aim is to help you make as informed a decision as possible.

There isn’t much to really talk about on either device because there is so much similar to last year. If you wanted to save some money, the most sensible thing would be to look back a year. Get either the Pixel 10 Pro or the iPhone 17 Pro. Save your money, get a new case, replace the battery, just make do and mend.

We’re here to discuss the merits, though, and while the gap at times feels quite large, I do think that Google has been diligently working on the Pixel lineup to the stage that most people will be very happy with their purchase. I hoped more would change, but there feels like some artificial brakes have been pumped this time on the Pixel 11 Pro. The iPhone 18 Pro is playing backup to the Duo this year, so it was always less of a priority for the company, even if it will be the biggest seller. 

Google doesn’t really have that excuse to lean on. All of the Pixel 11 phones are basically identical to the previous gen.

Then again, if we are being 100% honest with ourselves, does Apple deserve more criticism than Google for not moving the needle, given that the current crop of Pixel devices lacks a little more in certain key areas? It’s really frustrating to admit that, yes, there are more compromises on a Pixel 11 Pro than an iPhone 18 Pro across almost every area. The Pixel edges the iPhone in AI functionality and maybe stills photography, but the scoresheet isn’t exactly flattering.

To be blunt, this is not glazing the iPhone. It’s important to be objective, and objectively, you just get more for your money with the iPhone this year (again). No, I won’t be switching any time soon, and I likely won’t even keep hold of an iOS device this year, but in some ways, Apple deserves some plaudits as even without much change, the overall package still surpasses a similarly priced and similarly unchanged Pixel 11 Pro.

title: Rivian issues R2 recall for poorly tightened battery packs
snippet: The company says around 14 vehicles may be affected, and that it has resolved the issue on the assembly line.
fullText:
Image Credits:Rivian	

	

						

5:50 AM PDT · October 2, 2026

											

			

Rivian has issued a recall for its R2 SUV after the company discovered that fasteners on its high-voltage battery pack might not be properly tightened, which can cause a loss of power while driving. 

The company says only around 14 vehicles may have been affected, and that it will repair or replace damaged components on customer vehicles as needed. 

This is the second recall Rivian has issued for the R2, which started shipping to customers this year. It’s an all-important vehicle for the company, as it’s the first Rivian EV meant for a mass market and is supposed to help it reach profitability for the first time. The first R2 recall, issued last month, had to do with the visibility of the backup camera and was addressed with a software update.

In a filing, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) said Rivian first spotted the defect on September 17. A “manufacturing operator” at the company’s Normal, Illinois factory noticed one of the fasteners had been “under torqued” by an “automated station” on the assembly line. The company investigated and reprogrammed the station to reject “improperly torqued fasteners.”

Rivian told the safety regulator that it “is not aware of any customer reports, accidents, injuries, or fatalities

related to this issue.” Some Reddit users, along with RivianTrackr, a blog that follows the company closely, reported about the issue late last month. One owner said Rivian’s service department told them to stop driving immediately, and the company towed the vehicle.

Rivian has set an aggressive goal for the launch of the R2. The company has said it plans to ship between 20,000 and 25,000 of them by the end of this year. With deliveries starting in June, that would make it one of the fastest launches of a new EV in the U.S. market if Rivian pulls it off. The company is supposed to be adding a second production shift to hit those numbers, and has said early demand is strong for the new, more affordable SUV.

fullText:
The podracing scene in The Phantom Menace is one of my favorite movie sequences ever. It’s just so dang cool: The futuristic racers tear over treacherous Tatooine terrain while various Star Wars aliens bark at each other in incomprehensible sci-fi languages. Eventually a young Anakin Skywalker proves his mettle by clawing his way from the back of the pack to win the race, which left an impression on me when I first saw it at 10 years old. I always wished I could pilot a podracer myself. Over the past several days, I’ve been able to live out that dream thanks to Star Wars: Galactic Racer, which takes everything from that brilliant scene and packs it into a thrilling video game.

In Galactic Racer’s campaign, you play as Shade, a cargo pilot who gets a shot at racing in the underground Galactic League circuit to eventually challenge the smarmy champion Kestar Bool. The game is basically a roguelike. You start a run (called a “tour”) by picking between a few different vehicles — though you don’t get to drive a podracer until partway through the campaign — and selecting various perks that can influence your style of play. Races themselves take place across a few planets, including the desert Jakku planet from The Force Awakens, and you’ll pick different events to participate in from a branching map screen. After each race, you’ll get rewards to help craft your build, and along the way, you’ll also play brief sections where you walk around as Shade, talk with other characters, and upgrade your vehicle.

It’s all standard roguelike stuff, but the familiar format lets me better focus on the races themselves, which are really intense. Turns and obstacles that look far away come up in the blink of an eye, forcing you to react in an instant. Two different kinds of boosts mean you’re constantly surging forward in some way. And all the while, other racers are on the hunt, often ramming your craft or targeting you with weapons. I nearly always felt like I was just on the cusp of losing control, and a split-second mistake usually results in a crash. (When you crash, the whole game also briefly stops to showcase your wreckage flying across the track, which is satisfying in its own way.) Things get even more intense when you finally get into an actual podracer.

It’s extreme in the way that I imagined racing a vehicle in the Star Wars universe would actually be. There’s more to that feeling than the races themselves, though as developer Fuse Games — a relatively new studio with former staffers of Need for Speed, Burnout, and Star Wars Battlefront maker Criterion Games — makes the whole experience feel authentically Star Wars. The speeders and vehicles are grungy and worn, and your fellow racers constantly bicker at each other. (You’ll hear a lot of Huttese.) There are wipe transitions between scenes and bombastic, John Williams-esque music. My favorite touch might be the brief scene before each race where you press different buttons to prepare your vehicle, like what the racers do in The Phantom Menace.

That intensity also means that the campaign can be frustrating. I crashed a lot, often because I couldn’t see an obstacle in front of me until far too late, and the opposing racers can be extremely aggressive. I sometimes wished I actually had the reflexes of a Jedi to be able to keep up. A run can take a long time — late in the game, they can exceed two hours — which makes a late loss exasperating. Between tours, you can permanently boost your vehicle’s stats to make the next run easier, though that wasn’t always enough to make the pain of a loss worth it. Occasionally, I turned down the difficulty so that I could play without as much pressure.

Even after a brutal tour, though, I kept finding myself thinking about when I could carve out the time for another run. Galactic Racer isn’t the first Star Wars racing title, but it feels like the best realization yet of a game that embodies what made The Phantom Menace’s racing scene so memorable. I know I’ll never actually get to pilot a podracer, but Galactic Racer is close enough for me to live out my childhood dream.

Star Wars: Galactic Racer launches on October 6th on PC, PS5, and Xbox.

title: Lyft is paying $272.5M to settle lawsuit over how it classified drivers
snippet: Today, gig economy drivers are classified as contractors. This settlement clears up a lingering lawsuit from 2020 when that was still an unanswered issue.
fullText:
Lyft has agreed to pay $272.5 million to settle a lawsuit accusing the ride-hailing company of violating California law by misclassifying drivers as independent contractors, instead of employees. 

The company said in a regulatory filing that it believes the settlement will allow it to avoid the “costs and distraction of protracted litigation and enable management to maintain its focus on executing its business objectives.”

The settlement stems from a lawsuit filed by the California Labor Commissioner’s Office in August 2020 that accused Lyft of treating drivers as independent contractors rather than as employees, as required under state law at the time.

The lawsuit alleged that drivers were denied minimum wage and overtime, as well as other benefits and protections provided to employees, including paid sick leave and timely wage payments.

“This settlement is about the workers who came forward and spoke up. Their voices made this outcome possible,” California Labor Commissioner Lilia García-Brower said in a statement, adding that the LCO will forgo its share of the settlement and direct those funds to drivers who filed wage claims.

The settlement, which still must be approved by a judge, covers alleged violations from April 6, 2016, to December 15, 2020 — a period California was grappling with whether workers in the booming gig economy were independent contractors or employees.

Today, drivers for app-based transportation services like Lyft and Uber are classified as contractors after voters passed ballot measure Proposition 22 in 2020. The ballot measure provided a carve-out from Assembly Bill 5, a state law passed in 2019 that required companies like DoorDash, Lyft, and Uber to classify gig workers as employees, entitling them to minimum wage, workers’ compensation, and other benefits. 

Even after AB 5 took effect, Lyft, Uber, and other companies that relied on gig workers continued to classify their drivers as contractors. That eventually led to legal action from the LCO, California Attorney General, and the City Attorneys of Los Angeles, San Diego, and San Francisco, as well as private actions filed under California’s Private Attorneys General Act. The cases were coordinated in San Francisco Superior Court in September 2021.

“If approved, this settlement closes a chapter from a very different time, before Prop 22,” a Lyft spokesperson said in an emailed company statement. “The vast majority of rideshare drivers in California have always wanted to be independent contractors, and voters affirmed that when they passed Prop 22 in 2020, giving drivers new benefits and protections while preserving their flexibility. And since then, Lyft has gone further than Prop 22 requires, becoming the only rideshare company with a fee cap.

“Lyft believes drivers have always been properly classified under the law, and we’re glad to put this case behind us. We remain laser focused on helping create more earnings for drivers and more affordable rides for riders.”

The settlement closes this legal chapter, at least for Lyft. Uber still faces an LCO lawsuit that makes similar allegations.

title: tvOS 27 adds new reason to use profiles on your Apple TV 4K
snippet: Apple keeps improving its profiles feature on Apple TV 4K, and a change in tvOS 27 related to app access offers another reason to use profiles. more…
fullText:
Apple keeps improving its profiles feature on Apple TV 4K, and a change in tvOS 27 related to app access offers another reason to use profiles.

tvOS 27 lets you restrict users from launching specific apps

User profiles are a common feature of every major streaming service. They ensure viewers in a shared household can keep their viewing history and recommendations separate, among other benefits.

Apple has long had a profiles feature in tvOS, but it’s gotten a lot more useful in the past year thanks to several recent upgrades.

Now tvOS 27 has introduced another improvement. Per Apple’s official release notes:

Individual app controls in Settings let you block users from launching specific apps.

This change is clearly intended for parents. 

Profiles for children can already limit the types of content they’ll see in the Apple TV app. That’s a useful feature, but it won’t keep your child from opening a different app with no such restrictions.

	

Now though, parents can open Settings and block certain apps from being launched at all when a child’s profile is active.

It’s a good step toward making profiles as full-featured as they deserve to be, and aligns with Apple’s recent focus in iOS 27 on upgrading parental controls.

On the subject of profile improvements, iOS 27.2 and iPadOS 27.2 will bring Apple’s profile system to iPhone and iPad for the first time. You can read about that change here.

title: The ultra-pocketable ‘Picco’ e-reader from Boox is now up for pre-order, $99
snippet: The tiny e-reader form factor is starting to make a big splash as the company behind some of the best Android e-readers announces its own version Boox calls the “Picco,” now available to pre-order. more…
fullText:
The tiny e-reader form factor is starting to make a big splash as the company behind some of the best Android e-readers announces its own version Boox calls the “Picco,” now available to pre-order.

The Boox Picco has really only been teased here and there. We got a preview at IFA 2026, but we didn’t get to dive in as much as we wanted. The unit was still pre-production and in need of various refinements. Still, Boox has been in this game for a while, so we expect a good experience.

Today, Boox announced that Picco is now available for pre-order on its website. It starts at $99, but the website lists it at $109 for those purchasing from the US warehouse.

The Picco’s black-and-white display comes in at just 3.97 inches, and even still, it offers a front light for day and night reading sessions. It weighs just 58 grams, and even though Boox doesn’t list the device’s thickness in the press release, our own hands-on would tell us the tiny e-reader is plenty thin.

	

It will still add a little bulk to your phone if you choose to attach it with magnets. While it isn’t magnetic by itself, the Boox Picco comes with a case that makes it possible. It’s one of the most demanded features for the tiny e-readers that have already been released, because it adds a second screen without the doomscrolling and eye strain.

Another great detail to point out during the pre-order phase is that the Boox Picco doesn’t run Android, which we covered previously. This means access to third-party apps from the Google Play Store isn’t available. Still, a simple experience will allow users to transfer files with a companion app if you don’t want to use the SD card slot to manually move ePUB files.

Boox’s adorable little Picco is expected to ship out around October for those who pre-order.

fullText:
New Apple products are reportedly launching October 13, including the rumored ‘HomePad’ device. But according to Mark Gurman at Bloomberg, there’s one rumored product not coming next month: a new full-size HomePod with Siri AI.

Larger HomePod won’t be updated in October, but new version is coming ‘eventually’ per Bloomberg

Today Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reported that Apple plans to announce three new Home products very soon. 

New products coming include:

Smart home hub, commonly called ‘HomePad’

New Apple TV 4K

HomePod mini 2

Tuesday, October 13 is the expected launch date for each product.

But there’s one key Home product that isn’t coming in October. Gurman writes:

Apple aims to eventually update its larger HomePod speaker as well.

That’s the only mention he makes of the larger HomePod product, which hasn’t been updated since 2023.

	

Earlier this year, Gurman reported that a new full-sized HomePod was in the works alongside the updated HomePod mini and Apple TV 4K. When asked about their arrival, he said: “Just a matter of time. They’ve wanted to get the Apple Intelligence and new Siri features working in those products before rolling out the new versions.”

But despite Siri AI officially launching, and support being ready for the HomePod mini, it seems fans of the large HomePod will have to wait a while longer for a Siri AI-compatible hardware update.

Hopefully the wait won’t be too long, because in just a couple of weeks, the full-size HomePod will be the only Home product left that’s limited to the old Siri.

These are Messages features that Google announced or have been spotted in the wild by beta users.

Messages for web removing QR code pairing

Read receipts are now placed in a circle at the bottom-right corner of message bubbles and images. You swipe left to see timestamps and the encryption lock, while you can swipe right to reply. This first started appearing in August of 2024, but is now seeing wide beta and stable availability.

title: Google Messages rolls out new long-press menu with partial copying [Updated]
snippet: After testing got underway in January, Google Messages is finally widely rolling out a new long-press menu in conversations. more…
fullText:
After testing got underway in January, Google Messages is finally widely rolling out a new long-press menu in conversations.

Update 10/1: Google announced yesterday that the “new long-press redesign for Google Messages has officially launched.”

This update introduces a more intuitive way to interact with your conversations, featuring a tap-activated menu that puts your most-used actions front and center.

There’s also “full support” for light and dark themes, while the experience is now “optimized for landscape mode, ensuring the menu remains accessible and easy to navigate on wider screens.”

The company noted how the “ability to copy only a portion of a text message” was “one of the most requested features.” To do so:

	

Long press any message to bring up the new action menu.

Long press again directly on the text within that message.

Drag the selection handles to highlight the exact part of the message you want to select.

A second dialogue box will appear with options to Copy, Translate, or Select All.

Related: Google Messages rolls out new swipe for timestamps & reply gesture

Original 9/24: This new design replaces the top toolbar that housed various actions. Google only surfaced three actions with everything else in an overflow menu.

	

Upon long-pressing on a chat message or image, Google will show a floating menu with Remix (photos), Reply, Forward, Copy (text), Star, Delete, Select more, Info, and Save (photos).

Each action is accompanied by an icon at the front for quick scanning, while Copy lets you highlight a specific part of the message by pressing down and dragging the bubble. Previously, you could only copy the entire message.

If you’ve selected the newest message in a thread, Google will somewhat center it with a bouncy animation and haptic feedback. Messages prominently blurs the background layer when this menu is active. The row of emoji and “Create” Photomoji shortcuts is unchanged.

As of today, we’re seeing the new Google Messages long-press menu widely rolled out with stable version 20260910_03_RC02. There is a server-side component, so be sure to Force stop from the App info menu if it’s not yet live.

title: Twelve South launches tiny new ‘Airfly Drive’ wireless CarPlay adapter
snippet: Twelve South, the company behind a range of premium Apple accessories, has launched a notable expansion of its Airfly brand. The company today unveiled Airfly Drive, a dongle that turns wired CarPlay into wireless CarPlay. It’s available to order starting today for $39.99. Here’s how it works. more…
fullText:
Twelve South, the company behind a range of premium Apple accessories, has launched a notable expansion of its Airfly brand. The company today unveiled Airfly Drive, a dongle that turns wired CarPlay into wireless CarPlay. It’s available to order starting today for $39.99. Here’s how it works. 

Airfly Drive works with most cars that have factory-wired CarPlay, according to Twelve South. This covers more than 75 makes and model years back to 2014. Airfly Drive itself has a USB-A connector, but Twelve South includes a USB-C adapter in the box. It has a compact, aluminum design and is meant to stay plugged in. 

Twelve South’s Airfly Drive doesn’t require an app or account. You simply plug it into your car’s USB port, pair it to your phone once, and you’re set. Going forward, the Airfly Drive will automatically reconnect to your phone to enable the wireless CarPlay experience. It also supports two paired phones, controlled by a single button that switches between them. 

Twelve South outlines some specs and features: 

Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto on the car’s built-in display.

Plug-and-play setup with no app, account, or charging required.

Fast automatic reconnection every time the car starts.

One-press switching between two paired phones.

Compact aluminum housing designed to stay plugged in.

USB-A and USB-C support, with a USB-A to USB-C adapter included.

Works with the car’s existing display, buttons, and steering-wheel controls.

Ongoing compatibility updates.

Wireless CarPlay is significantly more seamless than wired CarPlay, especially for those shorter trips around town. It’s a great quality-of-life update for your CarPlay experience. 

You can order Airfly Drive from Twelve South today for $39.99. It’s available in black and white. It also works with Android Auto.

title: ESPN app recently got big upgrade on Apple TV 4K and iPhone
snippet: Fall is a big season for sports fans, and ESPN recently launched a big upgrade for users of its tvOS and iOS apps: 4K HDR streaming. more…
fullText:
Fall is a big season for sports fans, and ESPN recently launched a big upgrade for users of its tvOS and iOS apps: 4K HDR streaming.

ESPN streaming service now supports 4K HDR, with tvOS and iOS apps first to add support

In the last few weeks, ESPN began rolling out a big upgrade in its tvOS and iOS apps.

The streaming service now offers 4K HDR quality for top programming, including live games from the NFL, NBA, NHL, and more.

From ESPN’s press release last month:

This week, ESPN and ESPN2 will begin rolling out in 4K HDR in the U.S., elevating picture quality for fans during one of the highest stakes stretches of the year for live sports. This includes all ESPN productions of Monday Night Football, NBA and NHL plus select live events across college football and US Open tennis, and marquee live events like Super Bowl LXI. This update will deliver clearer edges, sharper colors and smoother movement — all critically important for delivering a richer and more immersive viewing experience for sports fans.

The ESPN App on iOS and tvOS will be the first to support the new experiences, with additional connected TV platforms to follow, as well as on Disney+ in the U.S. to ESPN Unlimited subscribers.

When browsing the ESPN app, you’ll see a new ‘4K HDR’ tag for content that supports the higher-quality video stream.

If you have a strong internet connection at home or on the go, 4K HDR will provide a more vibrant, crisp, premium image for your favorite sports content.

For any sports fans tempted to splurge on an Apple TV 4K for the first time, we recommend holding out just a little bit longer. The wait for a new Apple TV model is reportedly almost over.

Have you watched ESPN since it launched 4K HDR content? How did it look? Let us know in the comments.

fullText:
With Android 17 QPR2 Beta 6.1, HiLight on the Pixel 11 Pro series now supports message notifications.

When you go to a Google Contacts page, the HiLight bottom sheet shows options for Phone calls and Messages that you can individually enable/disable.

title: The founder’s guide to TechCrunch Disrupt 2026: Everything you need to know
snippet: TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 is built around one question: How do you build an enduring company in the AI era? Our programming and speaker lineup reflect that.
fullText:
TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 is built around one question: How do you build an enduring company in the AI era? Our programming and speaker lineup reflect that, based on the feedback we’ve gotten from the community and the reality on the ground.

Last year at Disrupt, we spoke with founders about their experiences and discovered the results of their attendance firsthand. One founder saw a 3x oversubscription rate after their confirmation for Startup Battlefield and more than 100 investor inbounds helping fuel conversations about a future fundraising round. Another founder had nearly 30 back-to-back conversations with investors who flocked to them after a pitch onstage and followed them to their booth.

That’s not the exception at Disrupt — that’s the point. And those opportunities aren’t just available for Battlefield finalists. Every conversation in the Expo Hall or in a Side Event can create an opportunity for your startup. For years, whether it’s been held in New York, San Francisco, or elsewhere, Disrupt has brought together thousands of founders, investors, startup team members, and tech leaders.  

We’re keeping that mission alive at SF’s Moscone West, this October 13-15 with a packed lineup of speakers, more than 200 expert sessions, a wealth of organized and serendipitous networking opportunities, and most of all, the chance to be in the same room as the person who could change your nascent idea for a company or your current startup’s trajectory.

This guide is for the founders out there who are just learning about Disrupt, who need a refresher, or are skeptical of whether it’s worth it. TechCrunch has been around for more than 20 years; we can take it. And before you dive in, we have two discounts that run up until Disrupt begins you should be know about. Founders can bring a team member along for 50% off their ticket by following this link, or you can help laid off members of your network find their next opportunity at Disrupt with our steep discount of Expo+ passes.

Image Credits:TechCrunch / Slava Blazer Photography

The reality of what makes Disrupt, Disrupt 

If you’re asking Claude or ChatGPT if TechCrunch Disrupt is worth it, you’re not alone. The reality is that Disrupt is a unique event, and it’s happening at a unique time for the startup community.

This year’s Disrupt isn’t about predicting the future of AI; it’s about building companies in it. Across six editorially curated stages, founders will hear practical lessons from the CEOs, investors, engineers, and operators shaping the next decade of technology.  

Whether you’re raising your first round, scaling your team, or deciding how AI changes your product, every session is designed to answer one question: “What can I take back to my company on Monday morning?”

The founders Disrupt empowers 

Disrupt works a bit differently, depending on where you are in your founding journey, with different tracks you can follow to make the most of the three days:

Pre-seed and idea stages 

You’re here to pressure-test your thesis, meet your first angel or pre-seed investors, and figure out who else is building in your space. Prioritize the Builders Stage, the Startup Battlefield semifinalist pitches, and the Expo Hall, along with roundtables tied to your industry and conversations you’ll want to learn more from.

Early revenue or actively raising 

You’re here for capital and validation above all else, and your time is valuable. Prioritize our investor-matchmaking tools and the connections that come with your Founder Pass, including the networking tools in our app. You also get access to the Deal Flow Café, where we foster one-on-one conversations between founders and investors.  

And when your schedule isn’t packed with dealmaking, learn from VC perspectives and fundraising-focused sessions at the Builders Stage.

Scaling, hiring, in search of partnerships 

You’re here in search of talent, strategic partners, and market visibility. Those same networking tools and opportunities can help you meet potential hires and partners and deepen those connections or make new ones. Disrupt’s Side Events aren’t to be missed — there’s one for every industry, interest, or post-event vibe you could be looking to find.

Startup Battlefield: The most iconic pitch competition 

The Startup Battlefield winner’s reveal packs the Disrupt stage and is each year’s capstone event. But it’s the lead-up to that $100,000 check and the deluge of attention the winner receives that’s the most valuable for founders attending Disrupt.

The 200 startups chosen on August 20 to compete go through a rigorous prep process and get the opportunity to pitch onstage in front of top-tier VCs and the Disrupt crowds. You’ll also get to watch those pitches, take notes, learn from the peaks and valleys, and potentially meet the teams behind the ideas and innovations. It could be in a follow-up meeting or just walking through the halls of Moscone.  

And if that all leaves you inspired, here’s an insider tip: Most Battlefield participants, and several winners, have gone through the process multiple times. We’re no longer taking applications for 2026’s competition, but we’re expanding the program to more international markets, and the 2027 process will be similar to this year’s, so take note for the future!

The founder-focused programming 

Disrupt 2026 spans several stages, each built around a different founder need:

Disrupt Stage: The biggest conversations in technology, featuring the founders, CEOs, and industry leaders defining what’s next. These are the conversations you’ll be talking about long after Disrupt ends.

Builders Stage: The tactical playbook for building a startup. From fundraising and hiring to GTM, product, and scaling, every session is designed to give founders practical advice they can put to work immediately.

AI Stage: AI isn’t the future — it’s the present. Learn how the fastest-growing startups are building, deploying, and monetizing AI, with practical lessons on agents, models, infrastructure, and what it takes to win in the AI era.

Real World AI Stage: AI is moving beyond the screen and into the physical world. Explore how robotics, autonomous systems, manufacturing, healthcare, and defense are turning AI breakthroughs into real-world products and businesses.

Smart Money Stage: Follow the money. From fintech and stablecoins to payments, embedded finance, and AI-driven financial services, this stage explores how technology is reshaping the movement of capital.

Smart Systems Stage: Every AI breakthrough depends on the infrastructure behind it. Discover the innovations in chips, compute, energy, networking, and data centers that will determine the next generation of technology companies.

Image Credits:TechCrunch / Slava Blazer Photography

Conversations you can only get at Disrupt 

RJ Scaringe (Rivian): Building a generational company. 

Panos Panay (Amazon): Designing products people love. 

Paolo Ardoino (Tether): Money, AI, and infrastructure. 

Toni Schneider and Rose Wang (Bluesky): Can social start over? 

Amjad Masad (Replit): Every founder becomes technical. 

Andrew Feldman (Cerebras): Winning the AI compute race. 

And that’s just the beginning — we’ll have more speakers to announce as we get closer to Disrupt. Check out the full lineup of speakers across all stages and events here.

How to get the most bang for your buck at Disrupt 

Disrupt’s prices increase as we get closer to the event, but we have a couple of promotions for Founders looking to save. You can save 50% on a second ticket by following the link here, and bring a coworker or co-founder along for the ride.  

If there are colleagues in your network who have been impacted by layoffs who you’d like to have join up, we have an option for them as well, with a special $75 Expo+ Pass available at a limited volume for those impacted by cutbacks this year.

Your time at Disrupt is valuable, too, so before you head there, check on our regularly updated schedule of speakers and Side Events, get ahead of competitors’ schedules by booking your networking opportunities in advance, and get your own elevator pitches in order to make the most of those magical Disrupt moments that can come at any point October 13-15!

title: Microsoft quietly ending ‘Copilot+ PC’ branding for Windows laptops
snippet: After a couple of years of relentlessly pushing it, Microsoft is seemingly ending its Copilot+ PC branding for Windows laptops. more…
fullText:
After a couple of years of relentlessly pushing it, Microsoft is seemingly ending its Copilot+ PC branding for Windows laptops.

Windows Central spoke with executives from Microsoft and Qualcomm about the lack of Copilot+ PC branding on the latest Surface machines. While it’s not been said explicitly, Surface CVP Brett Ostrum all-but-confirmed the end of that branding by saying:

…these are not called Copilot+ PCs. They do meet all the requirements of our previous bar for what Copilot+ devices are. We still lean into the narrative around AI on the edge and being able to have a hybrid solution out there.

	

Copilot+ PC branding was generally used to identify a laptop that met certain hardware requirements around AI features, particularly the NPU, which virtually every mid-high-end laptop already supports. Windows Central further points out that Nvidia’s RTX Spark push has been absent of any mention of Copilot+ PC branding.

Microsoft started using this branding back in 2024, but when the flagship feature of the Copilot+ PC, Recall, was met with backlash, the branding became little more than a hardware checkbox that consumers didn’t fully understand. 

	

The only big question left – does this mean the Copilot Key is going away?

fullText:
Apple debuted the all-new AirPods 5 this month, and they bring ANC to lower prices than ever before. If you’re shopping for AirPods, however, there are still several reasons you might want to opt for the more expensive AirPods Pro 3.

Buy AirPods Pro $234 (Reg. $249)

Buy AirPods 5 $129

Buy AirPods 5 with Wireless Charging Case $149

Different design

AirPods are one of Apple’s most personal products. The fit can vary dramatically between different people depending on the size of their ears. AirPods 5 offer an open-ear design, so they rest on the inside of your ear. AirPods Pro, meanwhile, offer a more traditional in-ear design with ear tips.

Personally, I find AirPods Pro to be more comfortable than AirPods 5. They’re also more secure for me, so I’m less worried they’ll fall out of my ears.

Heart rate monitoring

One of the key differentiators between AirPods Pro 3 and AirPods 5 is that AirPods Pro 3 offer built-in heart rate monitoring capabilities. During a workout, AirPods Pro can measure your heart rate to provide additional fitness metrics.

If you wear an Apple Watch, AirPods Pro 3 work along with your Apple Watch to ensure you get the most accurate data possible. Apple’s algorithms monitor the data from AirPods Pro and Apple Watch, and factor in the type of workout you’re doing, to use the most consistent data possible. For example, if you’re lifting weights and the Apple Watch ends up at an awkward angle on your wrist, AirPods Pro 3 will step in to provide more accurate data.

Furthermore, in iOS 27, Apple brought GymKit to the iPhone, so you can use iPhone and AirPods to get an Apple Watch-style experience … but without wearing a watch. Learn more about this change in Zac’s full coverage.

Hearing Aid

AirPods Pro 3 offer a range of hearing health features that aren’t available on AirPods 5. This includes:

Hearing Test

Hearing Aid

Hearing Protection

With the Hearing Test feature, you can take a 5-minute test to identify if you have hearing loss. Apple’s Hearing Aid feature, meanwhile, is a clinical-grade hearing aid that uses the results of your test to craft a sound profile for your needs. Finally, Hearing Protection, can help prevent exposure to loud environmental noise.

Wrap up

There are other reasons to choose AirPods Pro over AirPods 5, including longer battery life, even better ANC, and a more capable charging case. The difference in ANC, in particular, is notable: Apple says AirPods Pro 3 offer 3x more Active Noise Cancellation than AirPods 5.

fullText:

title: iOS 27 gives Apple Photos two features we’ve waited a long time for
snippet: iOS 27 is packed with new features for Apple’s Photos app, including two that have long been on many users’ wish lists: full-featured slideshow creation and upgraded iCloud Shared Albums. more…
fullText:
iOS 27 is packed with new features for Apple’s Photos app, including two that have long been on many users’ wish lists: full-featured slideshow creation and upgraded iCloud Shared Albums.

#1: Slideshow creation and customization

The Photos app has long supported a very rudimentary version of a slideshow feature. But it’s geared more toward reliving personal memories. If you wanted to create a slideshow for an event or other public viewing, you had to look elsewhere.

But in iOS 27, Photos finally adds a robust set of slideshow creation tools.

You can now play any set of photos or videos as a slideshow, customizing things like transition style, duration, and music. You can auto-loop the slideshow, and even save it as a video file for easy re-viewing.

Robust slideshow features are a long-overdue addition to the Photos app, but I’m thrilled that they’re finally here.

You may not know that the Photos app has its own social network-style feature: Shared Albums.

iCloud Shared Albums let you have an album that’s shared with friends or family. You get an activity feed to show new photos and videos that are added, and you have the option to like or comment on anything shared. It’s a lot like old-school Instagram, but private and limited to people you choose to share with.

I love the feature, and iOS 27 brings some long-awaited upgrades. You can now share full resolution photos and videos (they were lower quality before), react with any emoji, set new participant permissions, and Android and Windows users can now add photos too.

Shared Albums are improving just in time for Apple’s new HomePad device, and these upgrades make me even more excited for that product.
